records.context: Measure throughput and memory use to recommend a worker count.
records.label: spacr.benchmark#0
records.source: Measure throughput and memory use to recommend a worker count.
records.translation: Miðar yfirborð og minnslu notkun til að mæla vinnsluferli.

records.context: spaCR's worker defaults are arithmetic on the core count -- ``cpu_count() - 4``, ``cpu_count() // 2``, ``-1``. On a measurement run the core count is rarely the limiting factor: a microscope field of view is hundreds of megabytes decompressed, and eight workers on a 16-core laptop with 16 GB will swap long before they saturate the CPU. The limiting quantity is usually the memory one worker needs for one representative microscope field of view, which depends on the laboratory microplate and the machine, not on the core count.
records.label: spacr.benchmark#1
records.source: spaCR's worker defaults are arithmetic on the core count -- ``cpu_count() - 4``, ``cpu_count() // 2``, ``-1``. On a measurement run the core count is rarely the limiting factor: a field is hundreds of megabytes decompressed, and eight workers on a 16-core laptop with 16 GB will swap long before they saturate the CPU. The limiting quantity is usually the memory one worker needs for one representative field, which depends on the plate and the machine, not on the core count.
records.translation: spaCR vinnsluferli skilyrði eru arithmetic á kjarna reikning - ``cpu_count() - 4``, ``cpu_count() // 2``,``-1``. Á mælingum er kjarn reikning sjaldan takmörkandi tegund: mikroskópsvæðið er hundruð megabítum dekompressed, og átta vinnsluferla á 16-kjarna tölvu með 16 GB mun skipta lengi áður en þeir sýta CPU.

records.context: The benchmark therefore runs the real work over a few fields, records peak RSS and peak VRAM, and divides the available memory by the memory one worker used.
records.label: spacr.benchmark#2
records.source: The benchmark therefore runs the real work over a few fields, records peak RSS and peak VRAM, and divides the available memory by the memory one worker used.
records.translation: Þannig rennar skilaboðin raunverulegan vinnu yfir nokkrum sviðum, rekstur topp RSS og topp VRAM, og skiptir áætlað minningu með minningu sem einn vinnsluferli notaði.

records.context: **This measures; it does not tune.** It returns a recommendation and the evidence behind it, and never writes a setting. A benchmark that silently changed `n_jobs` would make a processing session's speed depend on when the benchmark last ran, which is the opposite of reproducible.
records.label: spacr.benchmark#3
records.source: **This measures; it does not tune.** It returns a recommendation and the evidence behind it, and never writes a setting. A benchmark that silently changed `n_jobs` would make a run's speed depend on when the benchmark last ran, which is the opposite of reproducible.
records.translation: **Þetta mæli; það tune ekki.** Það endurheimtir tilbeðingu og getu bak við það, og aldrei skrifa setting. Hugbúnaður sem þögulega breytist `n_jobs` myndi gera að hratt meðferð ákvarðan eftir hvenær hugbúnað síðast keyrir, sem er á móti endurnýjandi.

records.context: the highest resident set size seen, for the whole process. Not per worker -- the benchmark runs serially on purpose, so this is one worker's requirement.
records.label: spacr.benchmark.Measurement#3
records.source: the highest resident set size seen, for the whole process. Not per worker -- the benchmark runs serially on purpose, so this is one worker's requirement.
records.translation: Höfuðsta staðsett stærð er séð, fyrir allt ferli. ekki á vinnsluferli - skilyrði fer sérlega á tilgangi, þannig að þetta er þörf einn vinnsluferli.

records.context: A worker count and the retained evidence supporting it.
records.label: spacr.benchmark.Recommendation#0
records.source: A worker count and the retained evidence supporting it.
records.translation: A vinnsluferli tákn og beint vitni sem styðja það.

records.context: Return the worker count followed by its sizing explanation.
records.label: spacr.benchmark.Recommendation.__str__#0
records.source: Return the worker count followed by its sizing explanation.
records.translation: Hættu vinnsluferlinu eftir því að útskýringu hennar er mikill.

records.context: Available rather than total memory is used because total includes memory already in use; sizing workers against it can exhaust memory mid-run.
records.label: spacr.benchmark.available_memory_bytes#1
records.source: Available rather than total memory is used because total includes memory already in use; sizing workers against it can exhaust memory mid-run.
records.translation: Til staðar en summar minningu er notað vegna þess að summar inniheldur minningu þegar í notkun; stærð vinnsluferli gegn því getur eyðileggja minningu á miðjunni.

records.context: Items run serially because the recommendation divides by what one worker needs; a parallel run would measure the sum and hide that figure.
records.label: spacr.benchmark.benchmark#1
records.source: Items run serially because the recommendation divides by what one worker needs; a parallel run would measure the sum and hide that figure.
records.translation: Sérfræðingar rennast sérlega vegna þess að ráðleggingurinn skiptir eftir því sem vinnsluferli þurfa; parallel keyrir myndi mæta suminn og fela þessa tölvu.

records.context: Recommend a worker count from cores, free memory and measured usage.
records.label: spacr.benchmark.recommend_workers#0
records.source: Recommend a worker count from cores, free memory and measured usage.
records.translation: Vinsamlegast mæla vinnsluferli frá kerfi, frjáls minningu og meiddum notkun.

records.context: 1. Never more than ``cores``. More workers than cores is contention. 2. Never more than ``available memory - reserve`` divided by what one worker measurably needed. This is the term the core-count defaults omit, and it is usually the binding one. 3. Never fewer than 1, and never more than ``maximum``.
records.label: spacr.benchmark.recommend_workers#2
records.source: 1. Never more than ``cores``. More workers than cores is contention. 2. Never more than ``available memory - reserve`` divided by what one worker measurably needed. This is the term the core-count defaults omit, and it is usually the binding one. 3. Never fewer than 1, and never more than ``maximum``.
records.translation: 1. Aldrei meiri en ``cores``. Meiri vinnsluferli en kjarna er samræmi. 2. Aldri meiri enn ``available memory - reserve`` skipt af því sem einn vinnsluferli þarf meirið. Þetta er termin sem kjarn-kjarna skilyrði missa, og það er yfirleitt bindandi einn. 3. Aldrei minna en 1, og aldrei meiri að ``maximum``.

records.context: memory left for everything that is not a worker -- the GUI, the page cache the readers depend on, and the operating system. Defaults to 2 GiB.
records.label: spacr.benchmark.recommend_workers#3
records.source: memory left for everything that is not a worker -- the GUI, the page cache the readers depend on, and the operating system. Defaults to 2 GiB.
records.translation: minnu eftir fyrir allt sem er ekki vinnsluferli - GUI, síða skammsli sem lesendur eru að hætta, og vinnusystemi.

records.context: a :class:`Recommendation` carrying the reason, which states the limit that set the worker count.
records.label: spacr.benchmark.recommend_workers#4
records.source: a :class:`Recommendation` carrying the reason, which states the limit that set the worker count.
records.translation: a :class:`Recommendation` með ástæðu, sem sýnir takmörk sem setur vinnsluferli.

records.context: Label uninfected cells as bystanders or distal by distance to infection.
records.label: spacr.bystanders#0
records.source: Label uninfected cells as bystanders or distal by distance to infection.
records.translation: Label óþreyttar frumur eins og bystanders eða distal á fjarlægð til smitingu.

records.context: spaCR measures each cell on its own, but an infected cell can change the phenotype of its neighbours. Without a neighbourhood column, an uninfected cell touching an infected one and an uninfected cell on the far side of the microplate sample position are indistinguishable rows.
records.label: spacr.bystanders#1
records.source: spaCR measures each cell on its own, but an infected cell can change the phenotype of its neighbours. Without a neighbourhood column, an uninfected cell touching an infected one and an uninfected cell on the far side of the well are indistinguishable rows.
records.translation: spaCR mætur hvert frumu á sjálfum sér, en smitandi frumu getur breytt fenotypu nágrannanna síns. Án nágranna kolumna er óþekkt fruma sem ber á einum smitandi og óþekktu fruma á fjarlægum hliðum mikrópskrauna staðar óskiljanlegra ránum.

records.context: This has two consequences. A bystander phenotype cannot be detected, because no column separates a bystander from a distant uninfected cell. In addition, if bystanders are phenotypically shifted and pooled into "uninfected", the control population is a mixture: its variance is inflated and the effect size of every infection comparison is reduced.
records.label: spacr.bystanders#2
records.source: This has two consequences. A bystander phenotype cannot be detected, because no column separates a bystander from a distant uninfected cell. In addition, if bystanders are phenotypically shifted and pooled into "uninfected", the control population is a mixture: its variance is inflated and the effect size of every infection comparison is reduced.
records.translation: Þetta hefur tvö afleiðingar. A bystander fenotype er ekki hægt að uppgötva, vegna þess að engin stólur skiljar bystandera frá fjarlægum óþreytingu frumu. Að auki, ef bystanders eru fenotypislega breytt og tengt í "uninfected", stjórn populations er blanda: breyting hennar er uppflutinn og áhrif stærð á hverjum smitingu samanburði er minnkað.

records.context: The threshold is a length, not a pixel count. It is expressed as a multiple of the measured cell diameter, so it has the same meaning on a 20x and a 63x acquisition and on a plate whose cells are larger. A fixed micron value would suit one dataset and not the next.
records.label: spacr.bystanders#4
records.source: The threshold is a length, not a pixel count. It is expressed as a multiple of the measured cell diameter, so it has the same meaning on a 20x and a 63x acquisition and on a plate whose cells are larger. A fixed micron value would suit one dataset and not the next.
records.translation: Lágmargi er lengd, ekki tölur á pixelum. Það er útskýrt sem fjölbreytni af mættum celiðum, þannig að það hefur sömu þýðingu á 20x og 63x upphæð og á plötu sem cellernir eru stærri. A stöðugt mikrónum verð myndi passa einn gögn, en ekki næsta.

records.context: Label every cell infected, bystander or distal.
records.label: spacr.bystanders.classify#0
records.source: Label every cell infected, bystander or distal.
records.translation: Lætur á hverri smitandi frumu, bystander eða distal.

records.context: labels of the cells carrying a pathogen.
records.label: spacr.bystanders.classify#2
records.source: labels of the cells carrying a pathogen.
records.translation: Lítum af frumunum sem búa við sýkli.

records.context: how close an uninfected cell must be to count as a bystander, in the same units as ``spacing``. See :func:`reach_from_diameter`.
records.label: spacr.bystanders.classify#3
records.source: how close an uninfected cell must be to count as a bystander, in the same units as ``spacing``. See :func:`reach_from_diameter`.
records.translation: Hversu nálægt verður óvirkt fruman að tákna sem bystander, í sömu einum sem ``spacing``. Sjá :func:`reach_from_diameter`.

records.context: A non-positive reach makes every uninfected cell distal. This turns the bystander split off without a second setting, and a reach that is not a finite number is treated the same way.
records.label: spacr.bystanders.classify#6
records.source: A non-positive reach makes every uninfected cell distal. This turns the bystander split off without a second setting, and a reach that is not a finite number is treated the same way.
records.translation: A ekki jákvæða nálgun gerir hvern óþreytingu fruman distal. Þetta snúa bystander skilnað án aðra sett, og nálgun sem er ekki endilega fjöldi er meðhöndlað á sama hátt.

records.context: Count cells in each neighbourhood state, including empty states.
records.label: spacr.bystanders.counts#0
records.source: Count cells in each neighbourhood state, including empty states.
records.translation: Tölur frumur í hverjum nágrannalöndum, þar á meðal leyti ríkjum.

records.context: Every key is always present, so a caller comparing microplate sample positions receives 0 for an absent state rather than a ``KeyError``.
records.label: spacr.bystanders.counts#3
records.source: Every key is always present, so a caller comparing wells receives 0 for an absent state rather than a ``KeyError``.
records.translation: Hver key er alltaf til staðar, þannig að samtalandi sem samanburður brunnar staðsetningar fær 0 fyrir fjarverandi staðsetningu en ``KeyError``.

records.context: Distance from each cell to the nearest infected cell's surface.
records.label: spacr.bystanders.distance_to_infected#0
records.source: Distance from each cell to the nearest infected cell's surface.
records.translation: fjarlægð frá hverri frumu til nærustu yfirborði smitandi frumu.

records.context: ``label`` and ``distance_to_infected``, one row per cell.
records.label: spacr.bystanders.distance_to_infected#4
records.source: ``label`` and ``distance_to_infected``, one row per cell.
records.translation: ``label`` og ``distance_to_infected``, eitt stefnu á frumu.

records.context: An infected cell reads 0 and its immediate neighbour reads one pixel step, not 0. The field is zero on every infected pixel and grows outward, so a cell that shares a border with an infected one has its nearest pixel one step away: the minimum over that cell is 1. Only a cell whose own pixels are infected reads 0.
records.label: spacr.bystanders.distance_to_infected#5
records.source: An infected cell reads 0 and its immediate neighbour reads one pixel step, not 0. The field is zero on every infected pixel and grows outward, so a cell that shares a border with an infected one has its nearest pixel one step away: the minimum over that cell is 1. Only a cell whose own pixels are infected reads 0.
records.translation: Sjúkdómur hlýtur 0 og nærri nágranninn hans hlýtar eitt piksela skref, ekki 0. Reiturinn er null á hverjum smitandi pikseli og stendur út, þannig að fruman sem deila grænsi við smitinn hefur nærustu piksli sína eitt skref fjarlægð: mínimum yfir þessi frumu er 1.

records.context: Every distance is ``inf`` when the image has no infected cell, rather than 0 or NaN: infinity keeps `distance <= reach` False for every finite reach.
records.label: spacr.bystanders.distance_to_infected#7
records.source: Every distance is ``inf`` when the image has no infected cell, rather than 0 or NaN: infinity keeps `distance <= reach` False for every finite reach.
records.translation: Hver fjarlægð er ``inf`` þegar myndin hefur engin smitandi frumu, en ekki 0 eða NaN: Infinity halda `distance <= reach` False fyrir hverri lok.

records.context: Fraction of each cell's ``k`` nearest neighbours that are infected.
records.label: spacr.bystanders.neighbourhood#0
records.source: Fraction of each cell's ``k`` nearest neighbours that are infected.
records.translation: Fraction af ``k`` nærustu nágrannum á hverri frumu sem eru smitnir.

records.context: A cell is never counted as its own neighbour, and infected cells also receive a fraction, so an infected cell among uninfected ones can be distinguished from one inside a cluster.
records.label: spacr.bystanders.neighbourhood#7
records.source: A cell is never counted as its own neighbour, and infected cells also receive a fraction, so an infected cell among uninfected ones can be distinguished from one inside a cluster.
records.translation: Frumur er aldrei talin sem eigin nágrannalega, og smitnir frumur fá einnig fraktion, þannig að smitinn frumur meðal ósmitnir geta verið skilgreint frá einn inni klúster.

records.context: `neighbours_counted` is reported rather than assumed to be ``k``. A field with fewer than ``k + 1`` cells supplies fewer than ``k`` neighbours, and the column gives the denominator actually used. Fields with fewer than two cells return ``NaN`` fractions.
records.label: spacr.bystanders.neighbourhood#8
records.source: `neighbours_counted` is reported rather than assumed to be ``k``. A field with fewer than ``k + 1`` cells supplies fewer than ``k`` neighbours, and the column gives the denominator actually used. Fields with fewer than two cells return ``NaN`` fractions.
records.translation: `neighbours_counted` er talin í stað þess að það sé ``k``. Reiturinn með minna en ``k + 1`` kerfi veitir minna en ``k`` nágrannar, og stólinn gefur notandi sem virkilega er notað. Reiturinn með minna en tvö frumur endurheimta ``NaN`` frakkur.

records.context: Safe across execution paths, idempotent cancellation request shared with one worker.
records.label: spacr.cancellation.CancellationToken#0
records.source: Thread-safe, idempotent cancellation request shared with one worker.
records.translation: Sjálfur á leiðum til framkvæmd, ómögulegt hættu til að hætta með einn vinnsluferli.

records.context: This is a normal control-flow outcome, not a workflow failure.  Callers that catch broad :class:`Exception` values must throw the same exception again so the worker can record the processing session as ``cancelled`` rather than as a failed item.
records.label: spacr.cancellation.PipelineCancelled#1
records.source: This is a normal control-flow outcome, not a pipeline failure.  Callers that catch broad :class:`Exception` values must re-raise it so the worker can record the run as ``cancelled`` rather than as a failed item.
records.translation: Þetta er venjuleg stjórn flutning niðurstaða, ekki vinnuflutning mismunandi. Callers sem taka breiðar :class:`Exception` reikningar verður að kasta sömu undantekning aftur þannig að vinnsluferli getur skráð meðferð árangur eins og ``cancelled`` en ekki eins og mismunandinn hlutur.

records.context: Calls outside a managed worker are intentionally no-ops, so the same workflow functions work through the GUI, CLI, notebooks, and tests.
records.label: spacr.cancellation.checkpoint#1
records.source: Calls outside a managed worker are intentionally no-ops, so the same pipeline functions work through the GUI, CLI, notebooks, and tests.
records.translation: Rannsóknir út úr stjórnandi vinnsluferli eru ímynlega no-ops, þannig að sömu vinnufólks virkar í gegnum GUI, CLI, notebooks, og prófa.

records.context: The input consists of a guide- or gene-level coefficient, per-object measurements and per-microplate sample position guide fractions. Because pooled screening experiments do not identify which individual cell contains a guide, the result represents cells whose measured phenotype is consistent with the fitted effect; it does not assign a genotype to individual cells. :class:`MontagePlan` includes :data:`INFERENCE_NOTICE` in every generated caption to preserve this distinction.
records.label: spacr.cell_montage#1
records.source: The input consists of a guide- or gene-level coefficient, per-object measurements and per-well guide fractions. Because pooled screens do not identify which individual cell contains a guide, the result represents cells whose measured phenotype is consistent with the fitted effect; it does not assign a genotype to individual cells. :class:`MontagePlan` includes :data:`INFERENCE_NOTICE` in every generated caption to preserve this distinction.
records.translation: Inntakið består af leiðbeiningar- eða gen-næmi samkeppni, mættum per-object og per-microplate próf stöðu leiðbein fraktioner. Því að sameiginlegur skreynslu tilraunir skilja ekki hvaða einstaklinga fruma inniheldur leiðbeinn, niðurstöður er frumur sem mætt fenotype er samræmi við fitu áhrif; það er ekki að veita genotype að einstaklingum frumunum. :class:`MontagePlan` innihalda :data:`INFERENCE_NOTICE` í hverjum gerð útgáfu til að bjarga þessa skilning.

records.context: 1. :func:`wells_for_coefficient` identifies microplate sample positions with a non-zero fraction of the guide or gene. Gene-level selection sums guide fractions by default; :func:`select_montage_per_guide` evaluates guides separately. 2. :func:`score_window` defines ``target = baseline + effect`` and retains objects within ``half_widths`` robust scales of the target, ordered by ``|score - target|``. The baseline and scale are calculated across the supplied object population rather than separately for each gene. 3. :func:`objects_to_show` selects ``round(n_objects_in_well * guide_fraction_in_well)`` objects from each microplate sample position. Zero-contribution microplate sample positions remain in the plan for reporting.
records.label: spacr.cell_montage#3
records.source: 1. :func:`wells_for_coefficient` identifies wells with a non-zero fraction of the guide or gene. Gene-level selection sums guide fractions by default; :func:`select_montage_per_guide` evaluates guides separately. 2. :func:`score_window` defines ``target = baseline + effect`` and retains objects within ``half_widths`` robust scales of the target, ordered by ``|score - target|``. The baseline and scale are calculated across the supplied object population rather than separately for each gene. 3. :func:`objects_to_show` selects ``round(n_objects_in_well * guide_fraction_in_well)`` objects from each well. Zero-contribution wells remain in the plan for reporting.
records.translation: 1. :func:`wells_for_coefficient` ákvarða brunnar með ekki-zero flokk af leiðbeiningu eða génum. Gen-sjálf valkunar sumir leiðbeinar flokkum í skammt; :func:`select_montage_per_guide` er að mæla leiðbeinir sérstakt. 2. :func:`score_window` skilgreina ``target = baseline + effect`` og haldi hlutina innan ``half_widths`` sterka skammtur á markmiðinu, sem er beðið af ``|score - target|``. Baseline og skammur eru reiknað í gegnum veitt objektum fjölmiðla en ekki sérstaka fyrir hverja gén. 3. :func:`objects_to_show` velur ``round(n_objects_in_well * guide_fraction_in_well)`` hlutina frá hverri mikróbstæða stöðu.

records.context: Images are obtained through :class:`spacr.crops.PngCropSource` for exported PNG extracted image regions or :class:`spacr.crops.MergedCropSource` for extracted image regions extracted from ``merged/<fov>.npy``. :func:`resolve_montage_crop_source` reports when neither source is available. Per-well guide fractions are read from ``regression_data.csv``; the aggregate files ``grna_well.csv`` and ``well_grna.csv`` do not contain the required well-by-guide fractions.
records.label: spacr.cell_montage#4
records.source: Images are obtained through :class:`spacr.crops.PngCropSource` for exported PNG crops or :class:`spacr.crops.MergedCropSource` for crops extracted from ``merged/<fov>.npy``. :func:`resolve_montage_crop_source` reports when neither source is available. Per-well guide fractions are read from ``regression_data.csv``; the aggregate files ``grna_well.csv`` and ``well_grna.csv`` do not contain the required well-by-guide fractions.
records.translation: Myndin er tekin í gegnum :class:`spacr.crops.PngCropSource` fyrir PNG myndskurðir myndar svæðum eða :class:`spacr.crops.MergedCropSource` fyrir útgreiðar myndars svæðum útgreittar frá ``merged/<fov>.npy``. :func:`resolve_montage_crop_source` skýringar þegar engin útvarp er til staðar. Per-well leiðbeiningar er lesin frá ``regression_data.csv``; ``grna_well.csv`` og ``well_grna.csv`` geymir ekki nauðsynlegir skammtur.

records.context: Names are split into tokens (at ``_ - . space``, and failing that into digit and letter runs); the tokens that vary are found; one is tried as the image data channel -- or, when the user assigned image data channels, the tokens that only follow the image data channel are set aside -- and the rest must identify a set that holds exactly one image per image data channel. Each candidate is checked with :func:`check_sets` before it is returned. spaCR's own Yokogawa pattern is tried first and returned when it passes; :func:`spacr.regex_infer.propose` is tried last. Of the other candidates that pass, the one with the fewest image data channels is returned, the earliest on a tie, because a regex that reads each name as its own image data channel in a single set also passes the check.
records.label: spacr.channel_sorting.infer_regex#1
records.source: Names are split into tokens (at ``_ - . space``, and failing that into digit and letter runs); the tokens that vary are found; one is tried as the channel -- or, when the user assigned channels, the tokens that only follow the channel are set aside -- and the rest must identify a set that holds exactly one image per channel. Each candidate is checked with :func:`check_sets` before it is returned. spaCR's own Yokogawa pattern is tried first and returned when it passes; :func:`spacr.regex_infer.propose` is tried last. Of the other candidates that pass, the one with the fewest channels is returned, the earliest on a tie, because a regex that reads each name as its own channel in a single set also passes the check.
records.translation: Nafn er skipt inn í tokenum (ef ``_ - . space``, og missa að í tölva og bókstafur virkar); tokens sem breytast eru fundið; einn er reynt sem rás -- eða, þegar notandinn veitir rás, eru tóknir sem aðeins fylgja rás settar á undan -- og annar þarf að viðurkenna setur sem haldi nákvæmlega einn mynd per mynd gögnin. Hver sökandi er athugað með :func:`check_sets` áður en það er aftur. spaCR eigin Yokogawa mönnun er prófað fyrst og aftur þegar það fer; :func:`spacr.regex_infer.propose` er að prófa síðast. Af hinum kandidátum sem fara, þá sem með færsta mynd gögninna er aftur, fyrsti á tengslum, vegna þess að regex sem lesa hverri nafn sem eigin rás í einum setum fer einnig yfir athygli.

records.context: Every plate's measurements archive unpacks to ``measurements/measurements.db`` and every plate's extracted image region archive unpacks to ``data/`` -- the same two paths, four times over. records.translation: Þetta var venjulega einka ``^([A-Pa-p])[ _\-]?(\d{1,2})$`` með extra ``1 <= column <= 24`` athygli, þannig að ``Q01`` (ro 17) og ``A25`` (klór 25) - bæði fullkomlega góða brunna í 1536-laboratorium mikróbstæli sem heitumartöfn hefur þegar tekið - gekk aftur None og voru *endurnýjandi* til næsta frjáls syntetískra reikning. :func:`spacr.schema.parse_well` er nú parser, og :func:`spacr.schema.plate_format_for` ákveður hvort stöðu sem það framleiðir er mikróddstæður stöða sem er til.

records.context: Three conventions apply.  image data channel numbers are zero-based and diameters are pixels, so values copied from one magnification are not portable without conversion.  The default v1 mask workflow preserves the directory layout expected by downstream tools; ``pipeline_style='v2'`` is opt-in and writes a different streaming layout.  Finally, removing UMAP cluster noise also removes those objects from the returned frame, keeping the table and the visible embedding aligned rather than silently returning different samples.
records.label: spacr.core#11
records.source: Three conventions apply.  Channel numbers are zero-based and diameters are pixels, so values copied from one magnification are not portable without conversion.  The default v1 mask pipeline preserves the directory layout expected by downstream tools; ``pipeline_style='v2'`` is opt-in and writes a different streaming layout.  Finally, removing UMAP cluster noise also removes those objects from the returned frame, keeping the table and the visible embedding aligned rather than silently returning different samples.
records.translation: Þrír samningir gildir. rás tölur eru null-baseð og dýrmættir eru pixels, þannig að gildi kopið frá einum magnification eru ekki flytandi án breytinga. Þýskalandi v1 maska vinnu flutningin bjarga skýrsluna í hættu af downstream tólum; ``pipeline_style='v2'`` er opt-in og skrifa öðruvísi streikunar. Að lokum, fjarlægja UMAP klúster rök er einnig fjarlægur þessar hlutar frá aftur ramma, haldið tólinn og sýnileg innbyggingu sameiginlegt í stað þess að hlýtur aftur mismunandi tól.

records.context: This landing page currently serves two spaCR tiles.  **Mask** runs :func:`preprocess_generate_masks` to turn raw multichannel acquisitions into preprocessed arrays and Cellpose masks for cells, nuclei, pathogens, and organelles.  **Image UMAP** runs :func:`generate_image_umap` to reduce measured single-object features, cluster them, and optionally place representative extracted image regions on the embedding.  The same module also exposes the timelapse-mask entry point; the two main workflows remain independent, and UMAP does not segment images.
records.label: spacr.core#2
records.source: This landing page currently serves two spaCR tiles.  **Mask** runs :func:`preprocess_generate_masks` to turn raw multichannel acquisitions into preprocessed arrays and Cellpose masks for cells, nuclei, pathogens, and organelles.  **Image UMAP** runs :func:`generate_image_umap` to reduce measured single-object features, cluster them, and optionally place representative image crops on the embedding.  The same module also exposes the timelapse-mask entry point; the two main workflows remain independent, and UMAP does not segment images.
records.translation: Þessi landing síðu virkar í dag tvö spaCR tile. **Mask** fer :func:`preprocess_generate_masks` til að breyta rauð multichannel uppgötvun í fyrirframvinnu orðum og Cellpose maskar fyrir frumum, kjarna, sýkill og organelles. **Image UMAP** fer:func:`generate_image_umap` til þess að draga úr mættu ein-eðli eiginleika, klústa þá, og valframt sett representative myndskurðir myndar svæðum á innbyggðinu. Samur móddur sýnir einnig timelapse-mask innfangspunktur; tveir mikilvægustu vinnuflu eru sjálfstætt, og UMAP er ekki hluti af myndum.

records.context: Mask generation needs one or more source folders, a filename metadata scheme (``cellvoyager`` or an automatic/custom regex), zero-based image data channel indices for the objects to segment, and suitable object diameters and model choices.  At least one segmentation image data channel must be enabled.  Start with ``dry_run=True`` to validate paths, image data channels, models, and the planned writes without loading a model or changing the project.
records.label: spacr.core#4
records.source: Mask generation needs one or more source folders, a filename metadata scheme (``cellvoyager`` or an automatic/custom regex), zero-based channel indices for the objects to segment, and suitable object diameters and model choices.  At least one segmentation channel must be enabled.  Start with ``dry_run=True`` to validate paths, channels, models, and the planned writes without loading a model or changing the project.
records.translation: Maska kynslóð þarf eitt eða fleiri skáld, filenname metadata kerfi (``cellvoyager`` eða sjálfkrafa/specific regex), null-baseð image data channel sýningar fyrir objektum til segment, og viðeigandi objekt umfang og myndavél val. Að minnsta kosti einn skilyrði rás þarf að vera veitt. Byrjaðu með ``dry_run=True`` til að staðfesta leiðir, rás, tölur, og áætlað skrifa án þess að hlaða tölur eða breyta verkefnið.

records.context: The thumbnails overlaid on the embedding come from whichever extracted-image-region source ``crop_source`` names: ``'png'`` (and ``'auto'`` wherever an extracted image region folder exists) reads the pre-generated PNGs, ``'merged'`` (and ``'auto'`` with no folder) cuts each one out of ``merged/*.npy`` on demand through :mod:`spacr.crops`, so the embedding can be drawn on a project that never kept an extracted image region folder — ``png_list`` is not required in that case. Either way the pixels arrive through :mod:`spacr.crops`, so a legacy (pre-341f446) extracted-image-region folder is image data channel-corrected on load and the montage shows the same image the Annotate application view does.
records.label: spacr.core.generate_image_umap#2
records.source: The thumbnails overlaid on the embedding come from whichever crop source ``crop_source`` names: ``'png'`` (and ``'auto'`` wherever a crop folder exists) reads the pre-generated PNGs, ``'merged'`` (and ``'auto'`` with no folder) cuts each one out of ``merged/*.npy`` on demand through :mod:`spacr.crops`, so the embedding can be drawn on a project that never kept a crop folder — ``png_list`` is not required in that case. Either way the pixels arrive through :mod:`spacr.crops`, so a legacy (pre-341f446) crop folder is channel-corrected on load and the montage shows the same image the Annotate screen does.
records.translation: Tímar sem eru yfirleitt á innbyggingu koma frá hverjum myndskurði-mynd-region forrit ``crop_source`` nafn: ``'png'`` (og ``'auto'`` hvar sem myndskurður mynd-regionsfólkið er til) lesa fyrirframreidd PNGs, ``'merged'`` (og ``'auto'`` með engum skálum) sniður hver frá ``merged/*.npy`` á eftirspurn í gegnum :mod:`spacr.crops`, svo innbyggingu getur verið tekin á verkefni sem aldrei haldið út mynd svæðisfelli - ``png_list`` er ekki nauðsynlegt í þessu tilfelli. Einhver leið sem pixlar koma í gegnum :mod:`spacr.crops`, þannig að öryggi (pre-341f446) myndskurður-mynd-region mappur er rás-korrigir á loða og uppbyggingu sýnir sömu mynd sem Annotate app sýning gerir.

records.context: Given a source folder ``src`` of multi-image data channel images, this workflow (1) optionally consolidates inputs from nested folders, (2) renames files to the Yokogawa layout used downstream, (3) preprocesses per-image data channel arrays, (4) generates masks for cell / nucleus / pathogen / organelle image data channels via Cellpose (SAM variant), (5) optionally reconciles the cell mask against nuclei + pathogen overlays, and (6) writes overlay plots and a ``gen_mask_settings.csv`` next to the outputs.
records.label: spacr.core.preprocess_generate_masks#1
records.source: Given a source folder ``src`` of multi-channel images, this pipeline (1) optionally consolidates inputs from nested folders, (2) renames files to the Yokogawa layout used downstream, (3) preprocesses per-channel arrays, (4) generates masks for cell / nucleus / pathogen / organelle channels via Cellpose (SAM variant), (5) optionally reconciles the cell mask against nuclei + pathogen overlays, and (6) writes overlay plots and a ``gen_mask_settings.csv`` next to the outputs.
records.translation: Í bak við kjarntamál ``src`` af mörgum myndum gögn tákna myndum, þetta vinnufluðið (1) valframt konsolida inntökur frá hnítað mappum, (2) endurnýja skrif til Yokogawa áætlun notuð niðurstríð, (3) preprocesses per image gögnum táknar, (4) generates masks fyrir cell / kjarni / sýkill / organelle gögnin tákn með Cellpose (SAM breyting), (5) valframeslega samræma cell mask gegn kjörnum + sýkill overlays, og (6) skrifa overlay plots og ``gen_mask_settings.csv`` nálægt útgangi.

records.context: Planning and loading are separate. :func:`plan_crops` asks the database or the folder *which objects match* and reads no pixels at all: a ``COUNT`` and a ``SELECT`` of identifiers, or one ``scandir``. It is milliseconds on a plate of sixty thousand extracted image regions, so a screen can execute it on a click and tell the user what they asked for before committing to reading any of it. :func:`load_crops` then reads the pixels in pages, reporting after each one. A caller that executes the second half on a background execution unit gets a progress number per page and a stop that takes effect within a page rather than at the end.
records.label: spacr.crop_loader#2
records.source: Planning and loading are separate. :func:`plan_crops` asks the database or the folder *which objects match* and reads no pixels at all: a ``COUNT`` and a ``SELECT`` of identifiers, or one ``scandir``. It is milliseconds on a plate of sixty thousand crops, so a screen can run it on a click and tell the user what they asked for before committing to reading any of it. :func:`load_crops` then reads the pixels in pages, reporting after each one. A caller that runs the second half on a worker thread gets a progress number per page and a stop that takes effect within a page rather than at the end.
records.translation: Áætlun og loading eru mismunandi. :func:`plan_crops` spyr gögnum eða mappinn *sem hlutum tengjast* og lætur engin pixels alls: ``COUNT`` og ``SELECT`` af skilgreiningum, eða ``scandir``. Það er millisekundum á plötu af sjöutíu þúsund af myndum svæðum, svo skjár getur gert það með einum klukkustundum og segja notandi hvað þeir spurðu fyrir áður en að komast að lesa einhver af þeim. :func:`load_crops` lesa þá piksli í síðum, að skýra eftir hverjum. Kallandi sem fer á þriðja hálfi á bakgrunnsþjálfunum fær framtíðnum á síðu og hættu sem virkar innan síðu en í lok.

records.context: The input is either a ``measurements.db`` -- where the extracted image regions are chosen by object class, by plate, or by a predicate over ``png_list`` -- or a folder of extracted image region PNGs. The pixels come from :func:`spacr.crops.resolve_crop_source`, which decides whether to read pre-generated extracted image regions or cut them from ``merged/*.npy``, and a legacy folder is corrected on load as it is elsewhere.
records.label: spacr.crop_loader#3
records.source: The input is either a ``measurements.db`` -- where the crops are chosen by object class, by plate, or by a predicate over ``png_list`` -- or a folder of crop PNGs. The pixels come from :func:`spacr.crops.resolve_crop_source`, which decides whether to read pre-generated crops or cut them from ``merged/*.npy``, and a legacy folder is corrected on load as it is elsewhere.
records.translation: Inntakið er annaðhvort ``measurements.db`` - þar sem myndskurðir myndar svæðum eru valið af hlutklasi, af plötu, eða með fyrirspurn yfir ``png_list`` - eða mappur útgreiðsmyndar svæðis PNGs. Pixels koma frá :func:`spacr.crops.resolve_crop_source`, sem ákveður hvort að lesa fyrirframreiddar myndskurður myndar svæðinu eða skera þá frá ``merged/*.npy``, og öryggi mappurinn er korrigerður á loða eins og það er annars staðar.

records.context: The number of extracted image regions is capped by default. Sixty thousand extracted image regions of 96x96x3 take 1.6 GB before embedding, which can exhaust memory on a machine that could embed the first two thousand. :attr:`CropQuery.limit` therefore has a non-zero default, and the plan states what was left out -- "the first 2,000 of 61,433".
records.label: spacr.crop_loader#6
records.source: The number of crops is capped by default. Sixty thousand crops of 96x96x3 take 1.6 GB before embedding, which can exhaust memory on a machine that could embed the first two thousand. :attr:`CropQuery.limit` therefore has a non-zero default, and the plan states what was left out -- "the first 2,000 of 61,433".
records.translation: Þúsund þúsund myndskurðir myndar svæðum af 96x96x3 taka 1.6 GB áður en innbyggingu, sem getur eyðileggja minningu á vélum sem gæti innbyggð fyrstu tvö þúsunda. :attr:`CropQuery.limit` því hefur ekki-zero staðgreiðslu, og áætlunin segir hvað var yfirgefið - "fyrstu 2000 af 61,433".

records.context: Three counts are kept because rows are removed at two stages, for different reasons. ``matched`` is what the query found, ``selected`` is what the limit left of it, and ``count`` is what survived the merged route's join -- which drops every row with no single object label (``'omulti'`` / ``'onone'``) or no merged array recorded. Only the first gap is a cap, and only a cap is repaired by raising 'At most'; raising a limit that was not reached returns the same rows.
records.label: spacr.crop_loader.CropPlan#7
records.source: Three counts are kept because rows are removed at two stages, for different reasons. ``matched`` is what the query found, ``selected`` is what the limit left of it, and ``count`` is what survived the merged route's join -- which drops every row with no single object label (``'omulti'`` / ``'onone'``) or no merged array recorded. Only the first gap is a cap, and only a cap is repaired by raising 'At most'; raising a limit that was not reached returns the same rows.
records.translation: Þrír tölur eru haldið vegna þess að rán eru fjarlægð á tveimur stigum, af mismunandi ástæður. ``matched`` er það sem spurningin fann, ``selected`` er hvaða takmörk eftir það, og ``count`` er hvað lifði samskipti stefnu - sem droppar hver rán með engin einkefni merki (``'omulti'`` / ``'onone'``) eða engin samskipt rán er notuð. aðeins fyrsti hliðið er kapur, og aðeins kapur er endurtekinn með því að auka 'At most'; auka takmörku sem ekki er náinn mun aftur sömu ránum.

records.context: The extracted image region is padded, not resized: a stack has to be rectangular before a backbone sees it, and rescaling an extracted image region changes the apparent size of the object in it, which is a phenotype. Zero-padding changes the background, which is not. It is also what :func:`spacr.crop_source.crop_at` already does to a box that runs off the edge of a microscope field of view, so two extracted image regions of the same object arrive the same way whichever route cut them.
records.label: spacr.crop_loader.conform_crop#1
records.source: The crop is padded, not resized: a stack has to be rectangular before a backbone sees it, and rescaling a crop changes the apparent size of the object in it, which is a phenotype. Zero-padding changes the background, which is not. It is also what :func:`spacr.crop_source.crop_at` already does to a box that runs off the edge of a field, so two crops of the same object arrive the same way whichever route cut them.
records.translation: Mynd svæðið sem er myndskurður er padd, ekki endurnýjandi: Stack þarf að vera rektangulær áður en rygginn sé það, og endurskálingu af myndu svæðis breytist augljósandi stærð objekta í henni, sem er fenotype. Zero-padding breyta bakgrunni, Það er einnig það sem :func:`spacr.crop_source.crop_at` hefur þegar gert við boksi sem fer út úr vinstri mikroskóps., svo tveir myndskurðir myndar svæðum sömu hlutum koma á sömu leið sem hver leið skera þá.

Þjálfun áður notaði eigin skilyrði (``pre_generated`` / ``on_demand``) fyrir sömu val, þannig að notkun og þjálfun paneli sýndi einn sett undir tveimur setum nafn.

records.context: ``png`` — load pre-generated images (default) Read extracted image regions previously written by the measurement workflow. ``path_string`` filters paths by substring and ``file_type`` filters by image extension. This source performs no extracting image regions. ``merged`` — stream images Extract extracted image regions during training from ``merged/*.npy`` arrays. ``extract_channels`` selects the intensity image layers and ``object_array`` selects the labelled mask image layer that defines each object's extent. When ``coordinate_columns`` are configured, database coordinates instead define fixed bounding-box extracted image regions. ``generate`` — generate images, then load them Materialize a complete extracted image region set on disk before training, then read it through the same file-backed path as ``png``. This is a preprocessing action rather than a streaming source.
records.label: spacr.crop_source#2
records.source: ``png`` — load pre-generated images (default) Read crops previously written by the measurement workflow. ``path_string`` filters paths by substring and ``file_type`` filters by image extension. This source performs no cropping. ``merged`` — stream images Extract crops during training from ``merged/*.npy`` arrays. ``extract_channels`` selects the intensity planes and ``object_array`` selects the labelled mask plane that defines each object's extent. When ``coordinate_columns`` are configured, database coordinates instead define fixed bounding-box crops. ``generate`` — generate images, then load them Materialize a complete crop set on disk before training, then read it through the same file-backed path as ``png``. This is a preprocessing action rather than a streaming source.
records.translation: ``png`` — hlaða fyrirfram kynnt myndir (þekkt) Lesa myndskurð myndum svæðum áður skrifað af mælingar vinnuflokkinn. ``path_string`` filter leið með substring og ``file_type`` filter með myndarþekkingu. Þessi kjarn virkar engin myndskurði myndar svæðum. ``merged`` — Stream myndir Myndskurðinn myndar svæðinu á meðan þjálfun frá ``merged/*.npy`` rays. ``extract_channels`` velur stærð myndarklæði og ``object_array`` velja merkinn maska myndslæði sem ákveða umfang hvert objekt. Þegar ``coordinate_columns`` eru uppbyggð, databáðs samræmi í stað þess að ákveða stöðug tengsl-box myndskurðir myndarstöð. ``generate`` — gera myndir, þá laða þá Materialize fullkomna myndskurð myndar svæðið sett á skítan áður en þjálfun, þá lesa það í gegnum sama skáld stuðlað leið sem ``png``.

records.context: **Why streaming exists.** Pre-cutting every extracted image region writes a copy of the dataset to disk before a single epoch runs, and every change of extracted image region size or channel selection writes another. Cutting as training processing sessions costs a slice per object and no disk at all.
records.label: spacr.crop_source#4
records.source: **Why streaming exists.** Pre-cutting every crop writes a copy of the dataset to disk before a single epoch runs, and every change of crop size or channel selection writes another. Cutting as training runs costs a slice per object and no disk at all.
records.translation: **Hvers vegna streikingu er til.** Frá skreytingu hvert myndskurður myndareikning skrifa kopi af gögnum til skreyfina áður en einn þjálfunarlota fer, og hver breyting á myndskurði myndareiki stærð eða útgáfu skreyta annar.

records.context: **Bounding box versus object.** A bounding box is the smallest rectangle containing the object; an object-image-region masks everything outside it away. Both are useful -- the background around a cell is sometimes signal and sometimes contamination -- so it is a setting. Database-sourced objects can only ever be bounding boxes: a coordinate has no outline to mask against.
records.label: spacr.crop_source#5
records.source: **Bounding box versus object.** A bounding box is the smallest rectangle containing the object; an object crop masks everything outside it away. Both are useful -- the background around a cell is sometimes signal and sometimes contamination -- so it is a setting. Database-sourced objects can only ever be bounding boxes: a coordinate has no outline to mask against.
records.translation: **Bending box versus object.** Bending box er smáasta rektangle sem inniheldur objektinn; objekt-mynd-region maskar allt út um það fjarlægð. Bæði eru gagnlegar - bakgrunn um frumu er stundum signal og stundum sýning - þannig að það er sett.

records.context: This module is also the authority on **what an extracted-image-region PNG on disk means** -- see the "Crop PNG format" section below. In short: the current format is 3 ("declared_rgb", :data:`CROP_FORMAT_CURRENT`), whose red, green and blue slots hold exactly the source image data channels ``settings['png_channel_mapping']`` names; format 1 ("legacy", unmarked) holds the same bytes for the default mapping and is returned untouched; format 2, written for eleven days in 2026, is the one that is reversed, and :func:`read_crop_png` is what reverses it back. A folder says which format it is via a ``.spacr_crop_format.json`` sidecar, and an unmarked folder is format 1.
records.label: spacr.crops#11
records.source: This module is also the authority on **what a crop PNG on disk means** -- see the "Crop PNG format" section below. In short: the current format is 3 ("declared_rgb", :data:`CROP_FORMAT_CURRENT`), whose red, green and blue slots hold exactly the source channels ``settings['png_channel_mapping']`` names; format 1 ("legacy", unmarked) holds the same bytes for the default mapping and is returned untouched; format 2, written for eleven days in 2026, is the one that is reversed, and :func:`read_crop_png` is what reverses it back. A folder says which format it is via a ``.spacr_crop_format.json`` sidecar, and an unmarked folder is format 1.
records.translation: Þessi aðal er einnig mynd á **það er myndskurður-mynd-region PNG á skálum þýðir** - sjá "Crop PNG format" hluti hér að neðan. Í ljósi: núverandi formátur er 3 ("declared_rgb", :data:`CROP_FORMAT_CURRENT`), þar sem rauð, grænt og blá slottar halda nákvæmlega heild rás ``settings['png_channel_mapping']`` nafn; formátur 1 ("legacy", óþekkt) hefur sömu bítum fyrir skammt mappingu og er tilbúinn ótýkt; Formátur 2, sem er skrifað fyrir elfu daga árið 2026, er það sem er snúið, og :func:`read_crop_png` er því sem snúir það aftur. Fólkið segir hvaða formátum það er í gegnum ``.spacr_crop_format.json`` sidecar, og unmarked fólkið er formátum 1.

records.context: The intensity image data channels come first (the subset selected by ``settings['channels']`` at preprocessing time), then one ``uint16`` label-mask image layer per segmented object class, always in the order **cell, nucleus, pathogen, organelle** -- each present only if that class was segmented. ``settings['cell_mask_dim']`` / ``nucleus_mask_dim`` / ``pathogen_mask_dim`` / ``organelle_mask_dim`` record the resulting image layer indices; spaCR's default four-image data channel layout is ``{cell: 4, nucleus: 5, pathogen: 6, organelle: 7}`` (:data:`DEFAULT_MASK_DIMS`).
records.label: spacr.crops#6
records.source: The intensity channels come first (the subset selected by ``settings['channels']`` at preprocessing time), then one ``uint16`` label-mask plane per segmented object class, always in the order **cell, nucleus, pathogen, organelle** -- each present only if that class was segmented. ``settings['cell_mask_dim']`` / ``nucleus_mask_dim`` / ``pathogen_mask_dim`` / ``organelle_mask_dim`` record the resulting plane indices; spaCR's default four-channel layout is ``{cell: 4, nucleus: 5, pathogen: 6, organelle: 7}`` (:data:`DEFAULT_MASK_DIMS`).
records.translation: Intensi rás kemur fyrst (súsetur valinn af ``settings['channels']`` á fyrirframleiðslu tíma), þá einn ``uint16`` merki-mask gögn skál per segmented objekt class, alltaf í orði **cell, kjarni, sýkill, organelle** - hver núna aðeins ef þessi klass var segmented. ``settings['cell_mask_dim']`` / ``nucleus_mask_dim`` / ``pathogen_mask_dim`` / ``organelle_mask_dim`` skráðu niðurstöður myndslagsins; spaCR standað fjórum myndum rás áætlun er ``{cell: 4, nucleus: 5, pathogen: 6, organelle: 7}`` (:data:`DEFAULT_MASK_DIMS`).

records.context: :func:`extract_crop` reproduces the PNG path in ``spacr.measure._measure_crop_core`` step for step: same image data channel selection (``png_dims``), same region definition (object mask, optionally replaced by its padded bounding box, optionally dilated), same ``_crop_center`` centering/padding, same ``normalize_to_dtype`` percentile normalisation, same dtype. :func:`png_view` turns that array into what a consumer sees after the PNG round trip, and :func:`read_crop_png` reads an extracted-image-region PNG back into the same thing -- the two are the two halves of one contract, and ``tests/test_crops.py`` asserts they agree.
records.label: spacr.crops#9
records.source: :func:`extract_crop` reproduces the PNG path in ``spacr.measure._measure_crop_core`` step for step: same channel selection (``png_dims``), same region definition (object mask, optionally replaced by its padded bounding box, optionally dilated), same ``_crop_center`` centering/padding, same ``normalize_to_dtype`` percentile normalisation, same dtype. :func:`png_view` turns that array into what a consumer sees after the PNG round trip, and :func:`read_crop_png` reads a crop PNG back into the same thing -- the two are the two halves of one contract, and ``tests/test_crops.py`` asserts they agree.
records.translation: :func:`extract_crop` endurspeglar PNG leið í ``spacr.measure._measure_crop_core`` skref fyrir skref: sama rás valur (``png_dims``), sama svæðisgreining (object maska, valframt skipt af padd boðinum, valfritt breytt), sama ``_crop_center`` miðlun/padding, sama ``normalize_to_dtype`` semalegur staðfesting, sama dtype. :func:`png_view` breytist að tengja í það sem viðskiptavinur sé eftir PNG runda ferð, og :func:`read_crop_png` lesur út út afmynd-region PNG aftur í sama hlutinn - tveir eru tvö hálfa af einum samningunni, en ``tests/test_crops.py`` segir að þeir eru sammála.

Ískilinn kemur frá þessu mikroskópum sviði á sýn ``mask_dims``, ekki frá ránum, þannig að skilyrði key-value mapping sem nafnun á myndarklæði ránuna hefur ekki mismunandi hér en þögulegt grípað af mistökum litun.

records.source: plane indices in output order -- result channel ``k`` holds plane ``channels[k]``, and repeating an index repeats the plane. An empty sequence yields an ``(h, w, 0)`` array here; :func:`extract_crop` rejects it first.
records.translation: Myndslóðindika í útleiðslu - niðurstöður rás ``k`` holds myndslóð ``channels[k]``, og endurtekin indika endurtekið myndslæði. Hver verður að uppfylla ``0 <= c < C``; Neikvæðar sýningar eru nefndar í stað þess að vera hliðar, þannig að ``-1`` er mistök og ekki "the last plane". Öll sekúnd gerar ``(h, w, 0)`` hliðar hér; :func:`extract_crop` neita það fyrst.

records.context: Greyscale is preserved: when all three colours name the same source image data channel the result is a single image layer, so cv2 writes a one-image data channel PNG exactly as ``png_dims=[a]`` always did, rather than three identical image layers at three times the size.
records.label: spacr.crops.build_png_channels#2
records.source: Greyscale is preserved: when all three colours name the same source channel the result is a single plane, so cv2 writes a one-channel PNG exactly as ``png_dims=[a]`` always did, rather than three identical planes at three times the size.

records.context: The one translation from "what the user declared" to "what an extracted image region array holds". Everything downstream -- :class:`CropSpec`, :func:`png_view`, :func:`extract_crop` -- is in this order, so image data channel 0 of an extracted image region is always the red one and there is no second convention to keep straight.
records.label: spacr.crops.channels_from_settings#1
records.source: The one translation from "what the user declared" to "what a crop array holds". Everything downstream -- :class:`CropSpec`, :func:`png_view`, :func:`extract_crop` -- is in this order, so channel 0 of a crop is always the red one and there is no second convention to keep straight.
records.translation: Það eina þýðingu frá "what the user declared" til "hvað myndskurður myndar svæðis tengist". Allt niðurstríð - :class:`CropSpec`, :func:`png_view`,:func:`extract_crop` - er í þessari röð, þannig að myndar gögnin 0 af myndskurði myndar svæðinu er alltaf rauður einn og það er engin annað samning til að halda rétt.

records.context: A colour left empty has no source image data channel, so it cannot appear in a tuple of indices; it is filled with the first image data channel that *is* mapped, and the emptiness is applied later by :func:`build_png_channels`, which is the only place that can write a zero image layer. Callers that need the empty image layer honoured should use the mapping directly.
records.label: spacr.crops.channels_from_settings#2
records.source: A colour left empty has no source channel, so it cannot appear in a tuple of indices; it is filled with the first channel that *is* mapped, and the emptiness is applied later by :func:`build_png_channels`, which is the only place that can write a zero plane. Callers that need the empty plane honoured should use the mapping directly.
records.translation: A litur hægri hefur engin skýrmynd rás, þannig að það er ekki hægt að sýna í töflur af auglýsingum; Það er fyllt með fyrstu rás sem *is* geymt, og töluð er notað síðar af :func:`build_png_channels`, sem er eina staður sem getur skrifað null myndslett. Kallendur sem þurfa að völdu myndarklæði heiður ætti að nota mappingu beint.

records.label: spacr.crops.crop_settings_from_db#1
records.source: ``spacr.io._save_settings_to_db`` stores every setting as ``(setting_key, setting_value)`` strings; this parses them back so a crop cut on demand can use the same ``png_dims`` / ``png_size`` / ``normalize`` that produced the PNG folder.
records.translation: ``spacr.io._save_settings_to_db`` lagrar hvert sett eins og ``(setting_key, setting_value)`` ströndum; þetta skiptir þá aftur þannig að myndskurður mynd svæðis skortur á eftirliti getur notað sömu ``png_dims`` / ``png_size``/ ``normalize`` sem framleiðdi PNG mappinn.

records.context: The ``measure_crop`` settings. A scalar ``png_size`` defines a square extracted image region. Object-specific values in nested ``png_size``, ``dialate_pngs``, and ``dialate_png_ratios`` are selected by the object's position in ``crop_mode`` and fall back to the first entry when that object is absent. Channels are resolved from ``png_channel_mapping``, or legacy ``png_dims``, through :func:`channels_from_settings` and stored in colour order. Text forms such as ``"[2, 98]"``, ``"2,98"``, and ``"[1 99]"`` are parsed as percentile windows; a non-text sequence with a length other than two disables normalization.

records.context: 4 or more: **refused**. cv2 would write BGRA, and PIL then reads the fourth intensity image layer as an alpha image data channel and drops it on ``convert('RGB')`` -- a whole stain silently deleted from every extracted image region. ``settings['png_dims']`` documents a maximum of three entries; this is where a fourth stops being ignored and starts being an error.

records.context: Under the shipped rollback journal that combination starves the writer. A reader holds SHARED for the length of its statement, and a writer cannot COMMIT until every SHARED lock is gone, so with enough workers there is almost always someone reading and the committing worker waits out its busy timeout and raises "database is locked" -- usually surfacing on the next process's ``has_table``, which is the statement in the reporter's traceback.
records.label: spacr.database_concurrency.enable_wal_where_safe#2
records.source: Under the shipped rollback journal that combination starves the writer. A reader holds SHARED for the length of its statement, and a writer cannot COMMIT until every SHARED lock is gone, so with enough workers there is almost always someone reading and the committing worker waits out its busy timeout and raises "database is locked" -- usually surfacing on the next process's ``has_table``, which is the statement in the reporter's traceback.
records.translation: A lesendur halda SHARED fyrir lengd útskýrunar síns, og rithöfundur getur ekki COMMIT þar til hver SHARed lok er yfir, svo með nóg vinnsluferli það er næstum alltaf einhver að lesa og enginn vinnsluferli bíður út um upplifun sinn og heyrir "database is locked" - yfirleitt upp á næsta ferli ``has_table``, sem er útskýringinn í trackeback fréttamaður.

records.context: scratch database to create. It must not already exist (:exc:`FileExistsError`); missing parent directories are created, and a processing session that FINISHES leaves the file on disk along with any ``-wal`` and ``-shm`` sidecars, so every explicit run needs a fresh path. Omit it to probe a temporary database instead, which is removed after a clean finish. A processing session that RAISES -- a ``journal_mode`` :func:`connect` refuses, most often -- removes its scratch database either way: it never ran, so there is nothing in it to keep, and leaving one at an explicit path made the next run on it fail with :exc:`FileExistsError`. The one deliberate survivor is a worker that outlives the 30-second join deadline, whose database is kept for inspection.
records.label: spacr.database_concurrency.run_concurrency_probe#2
records.source: scratch database to create. Omit it to probe a temporary database instead, which is removed after a clean finish. A run that RAISES -- a ``journal_mode`` :func:`connect` refuses, most often -- removes its scratch database either way: it never ran, so there is nothing in it to keep, and leaving one at an explicit path made the next run on it fail with :exc:`FileExistsError`. The one deliberate survivor is a worker that outlives the 30-second join deadline, whose database is kept for inspection.
records.translation: Það þarf ekki að vera nú þegar (:exc:`FileExistsError`); mismunandi foreldrar skrifstofur eru skapaðir, og meðferð ákvarðan sem FINISHES yfirgefur skálinn á skálinu ásamt hvaða ``-wal`` og ``-shm`` sidekars, þannig að hver útskýrð þurfa nýtt leið. Óttast það til að prófa tímabata stað, sem er fjarlægð eftir hreint ferli. meðferð sem RAISES - a ``journal_mode`` :func:`connect` neita, oftast - fjarlægur skrafa gögn sama hátt: það hefur aldrei keyrslan, svo það er ekkert í því að halda, og yfirgefa einn á útskýrt leið sem framkvæma næsta ferli á það missar með :exc:`FileExistsError`. Ein hugsanlegur yfirleifandi er vinnsluferli sem lifir á 30-sekundum tengingu, sem gögnabata er haldið fyrir rannsókn.

records.context: spaCR processes batches — 384 microplate sample positions, thousands of microscope fields of view, dozens of image files. A single unreadable image must not abort the laboratory microplate, so almost every batch loop in the codebase wraps its body in ``try/except Exception`` and carries on. The historical problem was not the surviving; it was that the survival left no trace: forty microplate sample positions would fail to segment, forty lines would scroll past in a log nobody was watching, ``measurements.db`` would be written anyway, and every downstream regression would silently run on 344 microplate sample positions while reporting as if it had 384.
records.label: spacr.errors#1
records.source: spaCR processes batches — 384 wells, thousands of fields, dozens of image files. A single unreadable image must not abort the plate, so almost every batch loop in the codebase wraps its body in ``try/except Exception`` and carries on. The historical problem was not the surviving; it was that the survival left no trace: forty wells would fail to segment, forty lines would scroll past in a log nobody was watching, ``measurements.db`` would be written anyway, and every downstream regression would silently run on 344 wells while reporting as if it had 384.
records.translation: spaCR fer fram að skipuleggja - 384 brunnar, þúsund mikroskópstæðir sýningar, tíu myndir. Ein einhvers óreiðanleg mynd ætti ekki að brjóta mikróplátinn, þannig að næstum hver skipuleggjur í kóddabáði snúa líkama sínu í ``try/except Exception`` og fara áfram. Síðasta vandamálið var ekki yfirleitt; það var að yfirleiðan hættu engin spur: fjórða mikróplátstæði myndi missta að seggjum, fjórðum línum myndi snúa í gögnum enginn var að horfa, ``measurements.db`` myndi skrifað alls, og hvert niðurstríð regresion myndi slaka á 344 mikrorópstæði stöðum meðan tilkynna eins og það væri 384.

records.context: The workflow passes the response as one row per guide-in-well, but the response is a property of the well -- on the reference screen `log_pred` has exactly one distinct value in each of the 610 microplate sample positions, repeated once per guide the well retained. Counting every row would count a 15-guide well fifteen times and give n = 1,945 for 610 independent observations, overstating the evidence three-fold and weighting the distribution towards microplate sample positions with many guides.
records.label: spacr.figures.distributions.one_value_per_well#2
records.source: The pipeline passes the response as one row per guide-in-well, but the response is a property of the well -- on the reference screen `log_pred` has exactly one distinct value in each of the 610 wells, repeated once per guide the well retained. Counting every row would count a 15-guide well fifteen times and give n = 1,945 for 610 independent observations, overstating the evidence three-fold and weighting the distribution towards wells with many guides.
records.translation: Workflow yfirgefur viðbrögð eins og einn rán per leiðbeining-in-well, en svörin er eiginleika bólsins - á reference skjár `log_pred` hefur nákvæmlega einn skilgreinn gildi í hverjum 610 mikrópum próf stöðu, endurtekið einu sinni á leiðbeint brunnur beinni. Sumir hverri rán myndi tækja 15 leiðbeinn ból fimmtán sinnum og gefa n = 1,945 fyrir 610 sjálfstæðum athygli, yfirstaða gögn þriggja og þyngja sölu til mikróbum prófa stöðu með mörgum leiðbeinum.

records.context: **Unit of replication.** spaCR measures thousands of cells across a handful of microplate sample positions. Testing across cells when the replicate is the microplate sample position is pseudoreplication and can return p < 1e-10 on pure noise, because n is inflated about a thousandfold. Every result states what n counted, and :func:`compare` takes a ``unit`` so a caller can aggregate first.
records.label: spacr.figures.stats#5
records.source: **Unit of replication.** spaCR measures thousands of cells across a handful of wells. Testing across cells when the replicate is the well is pseudoreplication and can return p < 1e-10 on pure noise, because n is inflated about a thousandfold. Every result states what n counted, and :func:`compare` takes a ``unit`` so a caller can aggregate first.
records.translation: **Einstök replikarinnar.** spaCR Miðar þúsund frumur á milli mikróplata staðar. Testið á milli frumna þegar replicate er mikrópata staður er pseudoreplication og getur komið aftur til p < 1e-10 á hreinu hljóð, vegna þess að n er flóð um þúsund sinnum. :func:`compare` Að taka a ``unit`` Svo er hægt að hringja upp fyrst.

records.source: The output is a paragraph rather than a table: the coefficient table is already on screen and in a CSV. The paragraph states how many hypotheses were tested, how many passed and under which rule, which genes they were, whether the assay worked, and -- because the calibration on real screens is routinely off in one direction or the other -- whether the test was conservative or anti-conservative.
records.translation: Afleiðinginn er afsnit en ekki tabla: coeficienttabla er þegar á skimun tilraun og í CSV. Ástaðan segir hversu mörg hugmynd var prófað, hversu margir gerðist og undir hvaða reglu, hvaða gennir þeir voru, hvort prófun virkaði, og - vegna þess að kalibrering á raunverulegu skreynslu tilraunir er venjulega off í einum leiðinni eða annarri - hvort prófið var konservativa eða anti-konservativa.

records.context: The ``filters`` table: data-selection boundaries, written back to the database as columns.
records.label: spacr.filters#0
records.source: The ``filters`` table: gates, written back to the database as columns.
records.translation: Tabla ``filters``: gate, skrifað aftur til gögn sem kolumnar.

records.context: **Why a separate table.** The columns could be added to ``cell``, but a data-selection boundary is not a measurement: it is an interpretation, it is re-drawn often, and it belongs to whichever object the user was looking at. Writing into the measurement tables would mix the two, and re-data-selection filtering would rewrite a table that the measure step owns. ``filters`` is written only by this module, so it can be deleted and rebuilt at any time without losing a measurement.
records.label: spacr.filters#3
records.source: **Why a separate table.** The columns could be added to ``cell``, but a gate is not a measurement: it is an interpretation, it is re-drawn often, and it belongs to whichever object the user was looking at. Writing into the measurement tables would mix the two, and re-gating would rewrite a table that the measure step owns. ``filters`` is written only by this module, so it can be deleted and rebuilt at any time without losing a measurement.
records.translation: **Hvers vegna sérstaka tabla.** Sálin gæti verið lagt til ``cell``, en gate er ekki meirið: það er skilaboð, það er endurskoðið oft, og það er að hverjum hlutum notandinn var að horfa á. Skrifað í stærð tabla myndi blanda tveimur, og endurskoða gögn myndi endurskrifa tabla sem stærð stefnu eigandi. ``filters`` er skrifað aðeins af þessari mæli, þannig að það er hægt að fjarlægja og endurbyggja á öllum tíma án þess að missa mætti.

records.context: **The bootstrap.** The first data-selection boundary exported has to create the table, and the table has to carry enough identity that a filter can be merged back onto ANY object table or onto ``png_list``. spaCR joins those on ``plate / row / column / field`` plus the object label (and the timepoint, when the database is a timelapse), so those are exactly the columns :func:`build_filters_frame` collects -- from every object table present, not just the anchor, because a data-selection boundary drawn on nucleus measurements has to merge onto nuclei.
records.label: spacr.filters#4
records.source: **The bootstrap.** The first gate exported has to create the table, and the table has to carry enough identity that a filter can be merged back onto ANY object table or onto ``png_list``. spaCR joins those on ``plate / row / column / field`` plus the object label (and the timepoint, when the database is a timelapse), so those are exactly the columns :func:`build_filters_frame` collects -- from every object table present, not just the anchor, because a gate drawn on nucleus measurements has to merge onto nuclei.
records.translation: **Botstrap.** Fyrsta gate hringinn er útlendur til að búa til borðina, og borðinn þarf að bregðast nóg identity að fljótan getur verið tengdur aftur á einhverja gögn eða á ``png_list``. spaCR tengur þeim á ``plate / row / column / field`` plus gögn (og tímapunkturinn, þegar gögn er tímaband), svo þessar eru nákvæmlega gögn :func:`build_filters_frame` safnar - frá hverjum gögn þangað, ekki bara á hægri, vegna þess að gögnum-sálun hringurinn er tekin á kjörnum mælingum þarf að tengjast á kjarna.

records.context: Every object table contributes rows, not just the anchor. A data-selection boundary drawn on nucleus measurements has to merge onto nuclei, and a filters table built only from ``cell`` could not express that. Each object also carries an ``in_<table>`` flag saying which tables it appears in, which is what makes a merge predictable rather than a thing you discover by counting rows.
records.label: spacr.filters.build_filters_frame#3
records.source: Every object table contributes rows, not just the anchor. A gate drawn on nucleus measurements has to merge onto nuclei, and a filters table built only from ``cell`` could not express that. Each object also carries an ``in_<table>`` flag saying which tables it appears in, which is what makes a merge predictable rather than a thing you discover by counting rows.
records.translation: Allir hluttabla veita ránar, ekki bara anchor. Data-selection grændir þrátt á kjarna mótum þarf að fljúga á kjarna, og filter tabla byggð aðeins frá ``cell`` gæti ekki útskýrð það. Hver hlut bori einnig ``in_<table>`` flagga sem segir hvaða tákn það birtist í, sem er það sem gerir flókið fyrirvisað í stað þess að það er eitthvað sem þú uppgötva með því að tákna ránum.

records.context: One row per object of the FINEST kind present, carrying the label of each coarser object it belongs to. Flat rather than a link table per pair because every question asked of it -- "cells with more than three pathogens", "the mean pathogen intensity per cell" -- is a group-by on the parent, and a flat table answers those with no joins at all.

records.source: One row per object of the FINEST kind present, carrying the label of each coarser object it belongs to. Flat en tengslabíl per par vegna þess að hvert spurning sem spyrja um það - "frumur með meira en þrjá sýkill", "middar sýkill hærð per cell" - er hópur-by á foreldri, og fátækt borðið svara þeim sem ekki tengir alls.

records.context: Systematic on the row id, not ``ORDER BY RANDOM()``: random ordering sorts the whole table before discarding most of it, which costs more than reading everything. records.source: Systematic on the row id, not ``ORDER BY RANDOM()``: random ordering sorts the whole table before discarding most of it, which costs more than reading everything. Modulo á Ránum ID þarf einn pass og engin sorti, og er endurspegulegt - sömu röðum eru valið á hverjum tíma, þannig að gate grændir endurspega síðar situr á sama skugga af hlutum.

records.context: This is a merge onto the canonical structured-data names rather than a substitution for them because the canonical tables carry things a foreign table cannot reproduce: every spaCR feature column, and ``cell_id``, the link from a nucleus or pathogen back to the cell that contains it. Replacing the table would drop both, and a parent-child link is not recoverable from what is left. ``conversion_map`` gets the same treatment — merged on the output filename, never replaced — so a project's provenance back to its own original files survives an import into it.
records.label: spacr.foreign#13
records.source: This is a merge onto the canonical keys rather than a substitution for them because the canonical tables carry things a foreign table cannot reproduce: every spaCR feature column, and ``cell_id``, the link from a nucleus or pathogen back to the cell that contains it. Replacing the table would drop both, and a parent-child link is not recoverable from what is left. ``conversion_map`` gets the same treatment — merged on the output filename, never replaced — so a project's provenance back to its own original files survives an import into it.
records.translation: Þetta er samskipti við kanónískum byggð gögn-nafnum í stað þess að skipta fyrir þá vegna þess að kanonískum tólum búa hlutum en útlendur tól getur ekki endurspeglað: hvert spaCR tegundalvöru, og ``cell_id``, tengsl frá kjörnum eða sýkil aftur til frumu sem inniheldur það. records.context: 1. **Images** are scanned and planned by :mod:`spacr.convert` — the Yokogawa naming, the microplate sample position assignment and the ``conversion_map.csv`` come from there, unchanged. 2. **Masks** are scanned the same way and paired to microscope image fields of view. A proposal is not an application: it is what you save, edit and hand back. 4. **Columns are resolved** — collisions with spaCR names settled, unit conversions computed or refused. 5. **The join is verified** against the label images: every count in :class:`JoinReport` is measured from the masks.
records.label: spacr.foreign.plan_import#2
records.source: 1. **Images** are scanned and planned by :mod:`spacr.convert` — the Yokogawa naming, the well assignment and the ``conversion_map.csv`` come from there, unchanged. 2. **Masks** are scanned the same way and paired to image fields. A mask with no image and an image with no mask are both listed by path in :attr:`ImportPlan.masks`. 3. **Their table** is read and, when ``column_maps`` is not given, :func:`infer_column_map` proposes one. A proposal is not an application: it is what you save, edit and hand back. 4. **Columns are resolved** — collisions with spaCR names settled, unit conversions computed or refused. 5. **The join is verified** against the label images: every count in :class:`JoinReport` is measured from the masks.
records.translation: 1. **Images** eru skannað og áætlað með :mod:`spacr.convert` - Yokogawa nafnið, mikrópabandssamlinga staðsetningu og ``conversion_map.csv`` kemur frá því, óbreytt. 2. **Masks** eru skannað á sömu hátt og farin á mikroskópum myndum sviði. Maska með ekki mynd og mynd með ekki maska eru bæði listuð á leiðinni í :attr:`ImportPlan.masks`. 3. **Tabla þeirra** er lesið og, þegar ``column_maps`` er ekki gefið, :func:`infer_column_map` býður upp á einn. Tilboð er ekki notkun: það er það sem þú sparar, redigir og handur aftur. 4. **Columns eru leyft** — samræðingar með spaCR nafni sett, einkefni breytingar reiknað eða neitað. 5. **Snúð er staðfest** gegn merki myndum: hvert merki í :class:`JoinReport` er mætt frá maskar.

records.context: For a CRISPR screening experiment it is the penalised analogue of the mixed model with random effects -- "which genes are involved, where each gene is measured by several guides" -- and it addresses that question with no random effects, no REML fit, and no `gene_fraction` column. `gene_fraction` is the sum of a gene's guide fractions, so a design carrying both blocks is singular by construction. Here the gene enters as a grouping of the guide columns, never as a column of its own, so the design stays full rank.
records.label: spacr.group_lasso#5
records.source: For a CRISPR screen it is the penalised analogue of the mixed model with random effects -- "which genes are involved, where each gene is measured by several guides" -- and it addresses that question with no random effects, no REML fit, and no `gene_fraction` column. `gene_fraction` is the sum of a gene's guide fractions, so a design carrying both blocks is singular by construction. Here the gene enters as a grouping of the guide columns, never as a column of its own, so the design stays full rank.
records.translation: Fyrir CRISPR skimun tilraun er það gjaldt analóg blanda mynda með slæmt áhrifum - "hversgæna eru þáttur, þar sem hvert gæn er mætt af nokkrum leiðbeiningum" - og það ber við þetta spurning með engin slænt áhrifum, engin REML passa, og engin `gene_fraction` stólum. `gene_fraction` er sumurinn af leiðbeinarmálum gænna, þannig að hönnun sem búa bæði blokkum er einstakt af byggingu.

records.context: It also fits where OLS is undefined. This screen is 610 microplate sample positions and 823 guides; the penalty is what makes the answer well posed at p > n. A penalised fit therefore rests on the assumption that most guides have no effect; the penalty adds no new information.
records.label: spacr.group_lasso#6
records.source: It also fits where OLS is undefined. This screen is 610 wells and 823 guides; the penalty is what makes the answer well posed at p > n. A penalised fit therefore rests on the assumption that most guides have no effect; the penalty adds no new information.
records.translation: Þetta skjár er 610 mikrópabandstæður og 823 leiðbeiningar; ranga er það sem gerir svarið vel staðsett á p > n. Rangað ranga því á viðtalið að flestir leiðbeinir hafa engin áhrif, rangað bætir engin nýja upplýsingar.

records.context: Attribute a guide and a probability to every cell of a pooled screening experiment.

records.translation: Ákvarða leiðbeining og sannleika á hverjum frumum samsettu skreynslu tilraun.

records.context: A pooled screening experiment never observes which cell carried which guide: sequencing gives a fraction per microplate sample position. A guide with a measurable effect on the classification score shifts the scores, which allows cells to be attributed probabilistically.
records.label: spacr.guide_attribution#2
records.source: A pooled screen never observes which cell carried which guide: sequencing gives a fraction per well. A guide with a measurable effect on the classification score shifts the scores, which allows cells to be attributed probabilistically.

records.context: prior       pi_g        the guide's read fraction in the microplate sample position, normalised likelihood  f_g(s)      how likely this score is if the cell carries g posterior   r_ig    ∝   pi_g * f_g(s_i)

records.translation: A leiðbeiningur sem hefur lítil áhrif gegn breiðslu stigum getur aldrei náð takmörku, óttast um tölun frumur eða passa gæði.
