records.context: **Probabilities above 1 are clipped, with a warning.** The Bernoulli probability is a product of two independently drawn quantities and nothing constrains it to ``[0, 1]``; at ``alpha = 0.6`` the most abundant gene's share times a ``mu = 4.6`` microplate sample position factor exceeds 1 routinely. R's ``rbinom`` returns ``NA`` there and carries on. This clips to 1 and emits one :class:`AbundanceClippedWarning` carrying the number of clipped cells and the largest offending probability, because a clipped run has a realised genes-per-microplate sample position *below* the one that was requested — the answer is still usable, but not for the parameter value written on it.
records.label: spacr.power_simulate.simulate_spot_plate#3
records.source: **Probabilities above 1 are clipped, with a warning.** The Bernoulli probability is a product of two independently drawn quantities and nothing constrains it to ``[0, 1]``; at ``alpha = 0.6`` the most abundant gene's share times a ``mu = 4.6`` well factor exceeds 1 routinely. R's ``rbinom`` returns ``NA`` there and carries on. This clips to 1 and emits one :class:`AbundanceClippedWarning` carrying the number of clipped cells and the largest offending probability, because a clipped run has a realised genes-per-well *below* the one that was requested — the answer is still usable, but not for the parameter value written on it.
records.translation: **Sannleikur yfir 1 eru klippt, með varn.** Bernoulli sannleikur er vörur af tveimur sjálfstæðri þreytingu og ekkert takmarka það til ``[0, 1]``; á ``alpha = 0.6`` mest rennandi geins hlutverki tími a ``mu = 4.6`` mikróplata stafræna tegund er meira en 1 rútinn. R's ``rbinom`` kemur ``NA`` þar og fara áfram. Þetta klippur til 1 og útgáfa einn :class:`AbundanceClippedWarning` með fjölda klippta frumur og stærsta ógandi sannleikurinn, vegna þess að klippuð rún hefur raunverulegt gein-per-microplate stafrænni *undir* það sem var beðið — svarið er enn notuð, en ekki fyrir verðmæti á því skrifað.

records.context: The enhancement chain follows the same route. Make Masks' chain (:mod:`spacr.qt.detect_chain`) is written into a settings file as the ``enhance_*`` structured-data names and read back here by :func:`prepare_chain`, with the ``psf_*`` settings folded in as the chain's PSF stage, so one plate run applies exactly the steps a curator tuned, in the chain's own order: background, PSF, denoise, contrast, sharpen. The session applies it per selected channel at the stage the PSF already ran -- after illumination correction and before normalization -- and its provenance goes into the same ``psf/segmentation_application.json`` record, so a changed chain is refused on resume the way a changed kernel is. With no chain step on, a processing session is byte for byte what it was before the chain existed.
records.label: spacr.psf_pipeline#2
records.source: The enhancement chain follows the same route. Make Masks' chain (:mod:`spacr.qt.detect_chain`) is written into a settings file as the ``enhance_*`` keys and read back here by :func:`prepare_chain`, with the ``psf_*`` settings folded in as the chain's PSF stage, so one plate run applies exactly the steps a curator tuned, in the chain's own order: background, PSF, denoise, contrast, sharpen. The session applies it per selected channel at the stage the PSF already ran -- after illumination correction and before normalization -- and its provenance goes into the same ``psf/segmentation_application.json`` record, so a changed chain is refused on resume the way a changed kernel is. With no chain step on, a run is byte for byte what it was before the chain existed.
records.translation: Verksmiðjan er að fylgja sama leiðinni. Make Masks' ketti (:mod:`spacr.qt.detect_chain`) er skrifað í setningarfili sem ``enhance_*`` byggð gögn nafni og lesa aftur hér með :func:`prepare_chain`, með ``psf_*`` settingar fylgdu í sem PSF stefnu ketjunnar, þannig að einn plötur rennar viðeigast nákvæmlega skrefum sem kurator þunir, í eigin orði lánsins: bakgrunn, PSF ákvarðan, og neitað, og kontrast, og skarpa. Sessionin ákvarða það á ákveðnum rásum á steinu sem PSF hefur þegar keyrslan - eftir ljósi korrigeringu og áður en standalýsa - og útgangurinn fer í sömu ``psf/segmentation_application.json`` skrá, þannig að breytt ketti er neitað að endurheimta hvernig breytt kjarn er. Með engin ketti skref á, meðferð uppsetningu er byte fyrir byte hvað það var áður en ketti var til.

records.context: Spectral unmixing comes first. With ``unmix`` on, a bleed-through matrix is estimated from the single-stain control microplate sample positions ``unmix_controls`` names and every raw microscope field of view is unmixed across all its image data channels before illumination correction, the PSF and the chain; the matrix joins the same record. Measure estimates its own over the measured image data channels and unmixes each microscope field of view before its preprocessing hooks, recording the matrix in the saved processing-session settings and ``measurements/bleed_through.json``.
records.label: spacr.psf_pipeline#3
records.source: Spectral unmixing comes first. With ``unmix`` on, a bleed-through matrix is estimated from the single-stain control wells ``unmix_controls`` names and every raw field is unmixed across all its channels before illumination correction, the PSF and the chain; the matrix joins the same record. Measure estimates its own over the measured channels and unmixes each field before its preprocessing hooks, recording the matrix in the saved run settings and ``measurements/bleed_through.json``.
records.translation: Spektral unmixing kemur fyrst. Með ``unmix`` á, blæddur í gegnum matrix er uppgötvað frá ``unmix_controls`` nefnum einstaka litun stjórnun mikróplata staða og hvert rauðmikroscóp sviði er ekki blandað á öllum myndum rás áður en ljósi korrigering, PSF og ketti; Matrix tengist sömu rekstur. Miðar er eigin yfir mættu rás og blanda hverri mikroskópur sviði fyrir fyrirfram meðferð hók, skráð matriksi í sparað meðferð-session settingar og ``measurements/bleed_through.json``.

records.context: There is deliberately **no** ``worker.deleteLater``. The worker's affinity is the background execution unit, so a deferred delete is posted into a loop that is stopping, while the panel drops the object's last Python reference from the main GUI execution path — two owners, one object. ``bridge.make_thread``'s ownership essay records the gdb trace (``QThread -> sendPostedEvents -> ~QObject -> Sbk_GetPyOverride``) and the measurement: 3 crashes in 8 executions. A PySide6 object built in Python is already owned by Python; ``ConsolePanel``/``AIChatPanel`` hold it in ``_retired`` until the independent execution path has exited and free it there, on the independent execution path that holds it.
records.label: spacr.qt.ai.worker.make_stream_thread#5
records.source: There is deliberately **no** ``worker.deleteLater``. The worker's affinity is the worker thread, so a deferred delete is posted into a loop that is stopping, while the panel drops the object's last Python reference from the GUI thread — two owners, one object. ``bridge.make_thread``'s ownership essay records the gdb trace (``QThread -> sendPostedEvents -> ~QObject -> Sbk_GetPyOverride``) and the measurement: 3 crashes in 8 runs. A PySide6 object built in Python is already owned by Python; ``ConsolePanel``/``AIChatPanel`` hold it in ``_retired`` until the thread has exited and free it there, on the thread that holds it.
records.translation: Það er hugsanlega **no** ``worker.deleteLater``. Þannig er samstarfsaðili vinnsluferla bakgrundsins, þannig að slökkt fjarlægð er lagt í hlifun sem stendur, en panelinn drepur síðasta Python vísbendingu á hlutinn frá helstu GUI útgáfu - tveimur eigendum, eitt hlut. ``bridge.make_thread`` eigandi málsögur skráir gdb trace (``QThread -> sendPostedEvents -> ~QObject -> Sbk_GetPyOverride``) og mælingurinn: 3 flutningar í 8 útgáfum. A PySide6 hlutinn byggð í Python er þegar eigandi af Python; ``ConsolePanel``/``AIChatPanel`` haldið það inn ``_retired`` þar til sjálfstætt útgáfa hefur útgáf og það er frjálst á því, útgáfur sem það hefur.

records.context: optional callable asked before each image data channel's Cellpose model construction and forward pass. When it answers True the work is abandoned by raising :class:`OutlineCancelled`; ``'otsu'`` outlines are fast enough that they are never interrupted mid-image data channel.

records.source: optional callable asked before each channel's Cellpose model construction and forward pass. When it answers True the work is abandoned by raising :class:`OutlineCancelled`; ``'otsu'`` outlines are fast enough that they are never interrupted mid-channel.

records.context: A single substring matched with ``LIKE %x%`` can only require that a path contains a term. This grammar can also select the complement, for example the cells with no pathogen extracted image region (issue #7).

records.translation: Byggðu hágæna vinstri: Dock slott, skjár stack og stöðu bar.

records.context: Cooperatively drain analysis and UI workers before destruction.

records.translation: Samvinnuþróun og UI vinnsluferli áður en eyðileggjun.

records.context: A module folded into a host keeps its structured-data name everywhere a structured-data name is saved: a processing-session journal, the force-restart record, ``spacr-qt <app>`` in somebody's shell history. That structured-data name no longer names an application view, and navigating to it directly would build one -- an orphan page with no sidebar row, no tile and no way back to it.
records.label: spacr.qt.app.MainWindow.open_module#1
records.source: A module folded into a host keeps its key everywhere a key is saved: a run journal, the force-restart record, ``spacr-qt <app>`` in somebody's shell history. That key no longer names a screen, and navigating to it directly would build one -- an orphan page with no sidebar row, no tile and no way back to it.
records.translation: A mól sem er foldur inn í hýslinum halda uppbyggð gögn nafn þar sem uppbyggðar gögnum nafn er sparað: meðferð-sessíu dagblöð, krafta-upstart skrá, ``spacr-qt <app>`` í skál söguna einhvers. Þessi uppbyggða gögn nafnið nefnir ekki lengur við sýning á notkun, og að snúast á það beint myndi byggja einn - orphan síðuna með engin sidabarr, engin tile og engin leið til baka til það.

records.context: Build ``key``'s screen again, carrying ``values`` across.

records.translation: Búa ``key`` skjár aftur, með því að flytja ``values`` yfir.

records.context: settings to apply to the new screen.
records.label: spacr.qt.app.MainWindow.rebuild_app_screen#2
records.source: settings to apply to the new screen.
records.translation: Sættir til að gleyma við nýja skjár.

records.context: The whole screen is rebuilt because which settings a form holds depends on a few of its own values -- the organelle count, and whether an object's image data channel names an image layer -- so a committed change to one of those means a different form, not a changed one. Rebuilding is the same path every module open already takes.
records.label: spacr.qt.app.MainWindow.rebuild_app_screen#3
records.source: The whole screen is rebuilt because which settings a form holds depends on a few of its own values -- the organelle count, and whether an object's channel names a plane -- so a committed change to one of those means a different form, not a changed one. records.translation: Allur skæran er endurbyggð vegna þess að hvaða settingar forminn holds er eftir nokkrum af eigin gildi sínu - organelle tákn, og hvort rás á hlutinn nefnir myndslagi - þannig að viðeigandi breyting á einn af þeim þýðir öðruvísi form, ekki breytt einn.

records.context: The old screen is dropped from the cache and destroyed, so the new one is built from scratch rather than reusing widgets that belong to a shape that no longer applies.

records.source: The old screen is dropped from the cache and destroyed, so the new one is built from scratch rather than reusing widgets that belong to a shape that no longer applies.
records.translation: Gamla skjár er hættað úr cache og eyðileggið, þannig að nýja er byggð frá skratch í stað þess að endurnýta widgets sem tilheyra form sem er ekki lengur viðeigandi.

records.context: ``"module:function"`` of the callable the Run button runs. Resolved lazily by :func:`registered_entry` and consulted by :func:`spacr.qt.bridge.resolve_pipeline_entry`; without it the Run button answers "Not runnable".
records.label: spacr.qt.app.register_app#13

records.translation: ``"module:function"`` af hringandi keyrir hnappinn. Hlögðu með :func:`registered_entry` og skoðað með :func:`spacr.qt.bridge.resolve_pipeline_entry`; án þess svara Run hnoppinn "Not runnable".

records.context: Header displayed at the top of the application's screen. If omitted, it uses ``name``. Supply a custom header when the screen needs longer wording ("Illumination Correction" above a tile labeled "Illumination"). The value is stored in ``app_screen.APP_TITLES``.

records.source: header shown at the top of the app's own screen. Defaults to ``name``; give it only when the screen wants the longer form ("Illumination Correction" over a tile that reads "Illumination"). Reaches ``app_screen.APP_TITLES``.
records.translation: Header birtist á upphafi skrefnar á notkun. ef missað, notar það ``name``. Veita einkennilega header þegar skjár þarf lengri greining ("Illumination Correction" yfir tileð sem er merkinn "Illumination"). Verði er lagður í ``app_screen.APP_TITLES``.

records.context: Apps without a tile are not members. The result is what the tab draws and what its label counts, so a module with no tile is left out of both; otherwise the label would read "Results & QC (7)" over three tiles.
records.label: spacr.qt.app.section_members#1
records.source: Apps without a tile are not members. The result is what the tab draws and what its label counts, so a module with no tile is left out of both; otherwise the label would read "Results & QC (7)" over three tiles.
records.translation: Þess vegna er niðurstaða það sem taban tekur og það sem merki hennar talar, þannig að móddur með ekki merkjum er yfirgefið af báðum; annars myndi merkin lesa "Results & QC (7)" yfir þremur táknar.

records.context: ``APPS`` lists every registered app; this lists the apps Home draws a tile for. The two differ because modules fold into hosts -- a folded module keeps its registry row (it still has a screen, an icon, a section and a structured-data name to navigate to) and loses only its tile, because it is now reached from a button on its host or from the Help menu.
records.label: spacr.qt.app.tiled_apps#1
records.source: ``APPS`` lists every registered app; this lists the apps Home draws a tile for. The two differ because modules fold into hosts -- a folded module keeps its registry row (it still has a screen, an icon, a section and a key to navigate to) and loses only its tile, because it is now reached from a button on its host or from the Help menu.
records.translation: ``APPS`` listar hvert skráð app; Þetta er listan sem app Home taka tile fyrir. Þessir tveir eru mismunandi vegna þess að módúlar foldar inn í verksmiðjum - foldur módúnur halda rekstur sínu (það hefur enn skjár, tákn, hluti og byggð gögn-nafn til að sækja til) og tapar aðeins lítið sitt, því það er nú náð frá smá á veðri sínu eða frá hjálparmenni.

records.context: Anything asking "what does the user see on Home", "how many tiles are in this band", or "does this tile's label fit" wants this. Anything asking "can this key be navigated to", "does this app have artwork", or "does every app have a screen" wants ``APPS`` -- a folded module must still answer yes to all three.
records.label: spacr.qt.app.tiled_apps#2
records.source: Anything asking "what does the user see on Home", "how many tiles are in this band", or "does this tile's label fit" wants this. Anything asking "can this key be navigated to", "does this app have artwork", or "does every app have a screen" wants ``APPS`` -- a folded module must still answer yes to all three.
records.translation: Allt sem spyrja "það sem notandi sé á Home", "hversu margir reitir eru í þessum bandum", eða "tækir þetta reitirnir skilaboð" vill þetta. Allt sem spurir "þar að þetta key er að snúa til", "tökir þetta app hefur tegund", eða 'tökur hver app hefur skrin" vill ``APPS`` - folded module verður enn að svara ja til allra þremur.

records.context: :data:`DECLARED_APPS` is the canonical source for application names, descriptions, navigation sections, documentation links, and factory paths. Screen modules read their metadata from this catalog instead of duplicating the same strings.

records.source: :data:`DECLARED_APPS` is the canonical source for application names, descriptions, navigation sections, documentation links, and factory paths. Screen modules read their metadata from this catalog instead of duplicating the same strings.
records.translation: :data:`DECLARED_APPS` er kánonískur forrit fyrir notkunna, lýsingar, flutningssekningar, táknslum tengslum, og verkstjórnar leiðir. skjár móddur lesa metadata þeirra frá þessari sögu í stað þess að duplicate sömu strákur.

records.context: See :func:`spacr.qt.app.register_app` for what each field does once it is handed over, and :data:`spacr.qt.SELF_REGISTERING_MODULES` for the ordering constraint that decides *when* these rows are registered.

records.context: Run spaCR workflows in Qt workers and relay their progress to the GUI.
records.label: spacr.qt.bridge#0
records.source: Run spaCR pipelines in Qt workers and relay their progress to the GUI.
records.translation: Run spaCR vinnufluðum í Qt vinnsluferlum og flytja framgang þeirra til GUI.

records.context: :class:`PipelineWorker` executes a workflow call in a ``QThread`` and routes captured standard output and errors through ``line_ready``. The process-wide :data:`registry` tracks active jobs for shared surfaces such as Home, while ``make_thread`` centralizes worker registration and lifecycle setup.
records.label: spacr.qt.bridge#1
records.source: :class:`PipelineWorker` executes a pipeline call in a ``QThread`` and routes captured standard output and errors through ``line_ready``. The process-wide :data:`registry` tracks active jobs for shared surfaces such as Home, while ``make_thread`` centralizes worker registration and lifecycle setup.
records.translation: :class:`PipelineWorker` virkar vinnuflókna samtal í ``QThread`` og leiðir greiddur standa útgang og mistök í gegnum ``line_ready``. Process-wide :data:`registry` fylgir virk starf fyrir sameiginlegum yfirborðum eins og Home, en ``make_thread`` sentralizes vinnsluferli skrá og lífsýkrunarsetningu.

records.context: Stopping and pausing are cooperative. Every worker receives a :class:`spacr.cancellation.CancellationToken`, which long-running workflows poll at safe boundaries. :class:`PauseGate` and :func:`checkpoint` provide the pause protocol, but workflow entries that do not call ``checkpoint`` report ``supports_pause=False`` and must expose Pause as unavailable.
records.label: spacr.qt.bridge#2
records.source: Stopping and pausing are cooperative. Every worker receives a :class:`spacr.cancellation.CancellationToken`, which long-running pipelines poll at safe boundaries. :class:`PauseGate` and :func:`checkpoint` provide the pause protocol, but pipeline entries that do not call ``checkpoint`` report ``supports_pause=False`` and must expose Pause as unavailable.
records.translation: Hvert vinnsluferli fær :class:`spacr.cancellation.CancellationToken`, sem langvarandi vinnufluðum spyr á öruggum grænserum. :class:`PauseGate` og :func:`checkpoint` veita framhaldsprotokoll, en vinnuflaði innræðum sem kalla ekki ``checkpoint`` skýrslu ``supports_pause=False`` og verður að sýna Framhald sem óþægilegt.

records.context: worker allocation reserved in the processing session registry.
records.label: spacr.qt.bridge.PipelineWorker#15
records.source: worker allocation reserved in the run registry.
records.translation: vinnsluferli ákvarðanir eru undirritaðir í meðferðarafsins.

records.context: how many workers the processing session is allowed, passed through to the workflow rather than used here.

records.translation: hve margir vinnsluferli sem er leyft meðferð sinn, yfirgefið í vinnuflokk en notuð hér.

records.context: Lives on the main GUI execution path. ``progress`` is scraped from the worker's stdout (see :data:`_PROGRESS_RE`) rather than reported by the workflow, because the workflows have no reporting channel.

records.context: Extracted image region PNGs are not ordinary images. Anything spaCR wrote before the BGR fix has the first stain in the *blue* image data channel, and a 16-bit single-image data channel extracted image region opened with ``convert('RGB')`` is clipped to solid white by PIL. Both are corrected by :func:`spacr.qt.annotate_engine.load_crop_image`, which is therefore the only loader used here, so a hover preview shows the same colours as the annotation grid.
records.label: spacr.qt.crop_thumbs#7
records.source: Crop PNGs are not ordinary images. Anything spaCR wrote before the BGR fix has the first stain in the *blue* channel, and a 16-bit single-channel crop opened with ``convert('RGB')`` is clipped to solid white by PIL. Both are corrected by :func:`spacr.qt.annotate_engine.load_crop_image`, which is therefore the only loader used here, so a hover preview shows the same colours as the annotation grid.
records.translation: Myndregion PNGs er ekki venjulega myndir. Allt sem spaCR skrifaði áður en BGR fix hefur fyrstu litun í *blue* myndadata kanna, og 16 bits einn-myndadata-kanna myndskurð mynd svæðið opnað með ``convert('RGB')`` er klippt til fasta hvítan með PIL. Bæði eru korrigerðar með :func:`spacr.qt.annotate_engine.load_crop_image`, sem er því eina loader sem er notað hér, þannig að hover fyrirmynd sýnir sömu litum sem annotation gríðið.

records.source: The pixels and the record go in one call (:meth:`spacr.curation.MaskCuration.save_mask`), because either one alone misreports the file: a ledger beside untouched pixels claims corrections that were never applied, and labels with no ledger are a hand-edited mask nobody can tell from a segmented one.
records.translation: Pixels og rekstur fara í einu hringingu (:meth:`spacr.curation.MaskCuration.save_mask`), vegna þess að hvort sem einn misreportir skjölinn: Ledger ásamt ótýktum piksli segir réttlættir sem voru aldrei notuð, og merki með engum ledger eru höndraður maska, enginn getur sagt frá segmentiðum.

records.context: Mask generation applies the same chain. The image steps -- everything before ``detect`` -- are written as Mask settings by :func:`chain_settings`, one ``enhance_<field>`` structured-data name per :data:`SETTINGS_FIELDS` entry, and read back by :func:`spacr.psf_pipeline.prepare_chain`, which the V1 and V2 Mask workflows and the Mask Live preview apply to every selected segmentation image data channel after illumination correction and before normalization, at the stage the PSF already ran. Morphology and split act on a detector's labels and are Make Masks' own; a plate processing session's Cellpose labels are not reshaped by them. The Mask settings ``remove_background``, ``background`` and ``signal_to_noise`` are per-image data channel intensity floors applied by normalization afterwards, and :func:`spacr.object._preprocess_batch` is the organelle batches' own rolling ball and CLAHE; neither is configured here.
records.label: spacr.qt.detect_chain#8
records.source: Mask generation applies the same chain. The image steps -- everything before ``detect`` -- are written as Mask settings by :func:`chain_settings`, one ``enhance_<field>`` key per :data:`SETTINGS_FIELDS` entry, and read back by :func:`spacr.psf_pipeline.prepare_chain`, which the V1 and V2 Mask pipelines and the Mask Live preview apply to every selected segmentation channel after illumination correction and before normalization, at the stage the PSF already ran. Morphology and split act on a detector's labels and are Make Masks' own; a plate run's Cellpose labels are not reshaped by them. The Mask settings ``remove_background``, ``background`` and ``signal_to_noise`` are per-channel intensity floors applied by normalization afterwards, and :func:`spacr.object._preprocess_batch` is the organelle batches' own rolling ball and CLAHE; neither is configured here.
records.translation: Maska kynslóð á sama ketti. Skref mynd - allt áður en ``detect`` - eru skrifað sem Mask settingar með :func:`chain_settings`, ``enhance_<field>`` byggð gögn nafn á :data:`SETTINGS_FIELDS` inntali, og lesa aftur með :func:`spacr.psf_pipeline.prepare_chain`, sem V1 og V2 Mask vinnufluðum og Mask Live forritin gildir á hverjum valda skammsögn gögn tákn eftir ljósi réttlætis og áður en það er venjulegt, Í dag er PSF búinn að keyra. Morphology og split aðgerðir á merkingum uppgötva og eru Make Masks' eigin; Cellpose tákn í töflunarbreyfingu er ekki endurhaldur af þeim. Mask stillingar ``remove_background``, ``background`` og ``signal_to_noise`` eru styrkleiki á hverri myndargögnum sem beitt er með eðlilegum hætti eftir það og :func:`spacr.object._preprocess_batch` er eigin rúllandi boltinn og CLAHE;  er ekki stillt hér.

records.context: Morphology and the split both decide which pixels form one object, so both are applied to the detection as a whole: the labels are read as a foreground, reshaped, and labelled again. The ids therefore change, which costs nothing here -- Make Masks renumbers every object it pastes into a mask (:func:`spacr.qt.mask_engine._paste_region_objects`).
records.label: spacr.qt.detect_chain.finish#1
records.source: Morphology and the split both decide which pixels form one object, so both are applied to the detection as a whole: the labels are read as a foreground, reshaped, and labelled again. The ids therefore change, which costs nothing here -- Make Masks renumbers every object it pastes into a mask (:func:`spacr.qt.mask_engine._paste_region_objects`).
records.translation: Morphology og split bæði ákveða hvaða pixels sem tegund, þannig að báðir eru notuð á uppgötvun í heild: merki eru lesið sem fyrirfram, endurhæðist, og merkt aftur. IDs því breytist, sem kostar ekkert hér - Make Masks nefnir hvert objekt sem það fer í maska (:func:`spacr.qt.mask_engine._paste_region_objects`).

records.context: Those two lines, in that order, are reproduced exactly by ``tests/qt/test_gc_runs_on_the_gui_thread.py`` with no spaCR code involved at all: build a QObject that owns a *executing* QTimer, drop it into a reference CYCLE so only the collector can free it, then call ``gc.collect()`` from a background execution unit. The collector runs the destructor **on whichever independent execution path it happens to be executing on**, and Qt cannot stop a timer from there.
records.label: spacr.qt.gc_policy#2
records.source: Those two lines, in that order, are reproduced exactly by ``tests/qt/test_gc_runs_on_the_gui_thread.py`` with no spaCR code involved at all: build a QObject that owns a *running* QTimer, drop it into a reference CYCLE so only the collector can free it, then call ``gc.collect()`` from a worker thread. The collector runs the destructor **on whichever thread it happens to be running on**, and Qt cannot stop a timer from there.
records.translation: Þessir tveir ránir, í þessum orðum, eru endurspeglað nákvæmlega með ``tests/qt/test_gc_runs_on_the_gui_thread.py`` með engin spaCR kóða þátt í alls: byggja QObject sem eigir *executing* QTimer, kasta það í reference CYCLE svo aðeins samlarinn getur frelsað það, þá hringja ``gc.collect()`` frá bakgrunnsreiðslu. Samstæðingurinn keyrir destruktorinn **on hvar sem sjálfstætt útferð sem það gerist er að fara á**, og Qt getur ekki stoppað tímar frá því.

records.context: The defect is not specific to the preview. CPython runs an automatic collection whenever an allocation pushes a generation past its threshold, so the collection executes on the independent execution path that allocated most recently. A Cellpose pass allocates heavily in a background execution unit, so that worker is the likely independent execution path to execute the collection and therefore to destroy unrelated widgets the main GUI execution path released earlier. The resulting crash is timing-dependent, occurs away from the code that created the cycle, and names no file.
records.label: spacr.qt.gc_policy#3
records.source: The defect is not specific to the preview. CPython runs an automatic collection whenever an allocation pushes a generation past its threshold, so the collection runs on the thread that allocated most recently. A Cellpose pass allocates heavily in a worker thread, so that worker is the likely thread to run the collection and therefore to destroy unrelated widgets the GUI thread released earlier. The resulting crash is timing-dependent, occurs away from the code that created the cycle, and names no file.
records.translation: Svona er ekki sérstök fyrir forrit. CPython keyrir sjálfkrafa safnað þegar aðstoð dreyma kynslóð yfir takmörk sitt, þannig að safnað fer á sjálfstætt framkvæmd stefnu sem er aðstoðað síðast. A Cellpose pass er þyngd aðstoðar í bakgrunni framkvæmd einkefni, svo að vinnsluferli er líklega sjálfstæð framkvæmd leið til að fara upp safnað og því að eyða óhætt widgets aðsta GUI framkvæmds stefnu birtist áður.

records.context: A combo box whose entries a handler reads back with ``currentText()`` cannot be translated: the caption moves and every comparison misses. That is why the live preview's dropdowns were marked untranslatable outright, and why the ones that were not marked went wrong quietly -- the segmentation object box handed ``cellen`` to a worker that only knows ``cell``, and the threshold method wrote ``medelvärde`` into a setting name that only accepts ``mean``.

records.source: A combo box whose entries a handler reads back with ``currentText()`` cannot be translated: the caption moves and every comparison misses. records.translation: A kombo boksi sem innræðir viðskiptavini lesa aftur með ``currentText()`` er ekki hægt að þýða: viðbótin fer og hvert samræmi missa. Það er ástæðan fyrir því að niðurstöður á live preview voru merkt óþreytandi augnablik, og hvers vegna þeir sem voru ekki merkt fóru rangt þægilega - segmentað efni boði gefur ``cellen`` vinnsluferlum sem þekkja aðeins ``cell``, og gríðsmetan skrifaði ``medelvärde`` í setting nafn sem samþykkir aðeins ``mean``.

records.context: The cached value lasts for one scope, not for the process. A permanent cache would keep a language the user has just changed; inside a single synchronous build the language cannot change, because nothing else runs between the calls. records.label: spacr.qt.i18n.ui_language_resolved_once#2
records.source: The cached value lasts for one scope, not for the process. A permanent cache would keep a language the user has just changed; inside a single synchronous build the language cannot change, because nothing else runs between the calls. Nested scopes share the outermost dict and only the outermost discards it, so a screen that wraps its whole build and a helper that wraps itself use the same cached value.
records.translation: Hugmyndin er á einum sviði, ekki á ferli. A stöðugt cache myndi halda tungumál sem notandi hefur bara breytt; inn í einum synkrónum byggingu tungumálin getur ekki breyst, vegna þess að ekkert annað fer á milli samtal. Nested scopes deila hærsta key-value mapping og aðeins hærst discardir það, þannig að skjár sem snúa allan bygginginn og hjálparinn sem snúir sjálfan sig nota sama cached gildi.

records.context: The old behaviour here was ``label(mask > 0)``, which renumbers the connected components 1..N on every save. records.source: The old behaviour here was ``label(mask > 0)``, which renumbers the connected components 1..N on every save. Það kasta fjarlægð einstaklinga af hverjum hlutum: eyðileggja hlut 7 af 20 og hlut 8..20 hver slide niður fyrir einn, þannig að safnað maska ekki lengur byggð-data-nafn gegn mótum, myndskurðir myndar svæðum eða stigum sem uppgötvunar það var beint frá.

records.context: **A mask with one foreground value carries no ids to keep.** That is what a purely brush-painted mask looks like -- every stroke writes the same value -- and it is a binary image, not a label image. Its components are numbered 1..N, which loses nothing.

records.source: **A mask with one foreground value carries no ids to keep.** That is what a purely brush-painted mask looks like -- every stroke writes the same value -- and it is a binary image, not a label image. Its components are numbered 1..N, which loses nothing.

records.context: **A label that names two separated blobs is split.** One id must mean one object. records.label: spacr.qt.mask_engine.canonical_labels#4
records.source: **A label that names two separated blobs is split.** One id must mean one object. records.translation: **A merki sem heitir tveimur skilgreiðum blóbum er skilað.** Einn ID verður að þýða eitt objekt. Stærsta hluti halda ID og resturinn er gefið minnsta IDs ekki þegar í notkun, þannig að tegund annað blób með brús yfir raunverulegu segmenningu bætir objekt í stað þess að breyta fjarlæg einn.

records.context: This is the tool a brush is not. A brush stamps disks along the path, so tracing a cell's rim with it labels the rim and leaves the middle background; ``draw`` closes the path (last point back to the first) and fills what it encloses, so one gesture produces one solid object with one id. Anything already labelled inside the outline is overwritten, which is the point: the outline asserts "all of this is one object".
records.label: spacr.qt.mask_engine.fill_polygon#1
records.source: This is the tool a brush is not. A brush stamps disks along the path, so tracing a cell's rim with it labels the rim and leaves the middle background; ``draw`` closes the path (last point back to the first) and fills what it encloses, so one gesture produces one solid object with one id. Anything already labelled inside the outline is overwritten, which is the point: the outline asserts "all of this is one object".
records.translation: Þetta er aðstoð brús er ekki. brús stempur skálum langs leiðinni, þannig að spyrja rímur fruman með það merktir ríminn og yfirgefur miðjunni bakgrunni; ``draw`` fer ferlið (úlsta punktur aftur til fyrstu) og fylgir það sem það fer, svo einn gestur framleiðir einn sól objekt með einn ID. Allt sem hefur verið merkt inn í útliti er yfirskript, sem er punkturinn: útlitið segir "allega þetta er eitt objekt".

records.context: The banner **reads** a verdict; it does not compute one.  Opening a plate's masks takes seconds to minutes, which is too slow for every visit to the screen.  So :func:`spacr.seg_qc.read_digest` parses the CSVs the mask run already wrote, dates each one against its mask stack, and reports a card older than its masks as out of date instead of using it.  Only the *Score the masks now* button scores anything, only when pressed, and it does it on a background execution unit and writes the card so the next open is cheap again.
records.label: spacr.qt.prerun#6
records.source: The banner **reads** a verdict; it does not compute one.  Opening a plate's masks takes seconds to minutes, which is too slow for every visit to the screen.  So :func:`spacr.seg_qc.read_digest` parses the CSVs the mask run already wrote, dates each one against its mask stack, and reports a card older than its masks as out of date instead of using it.  Only the *Score the masks now* button scores anything, only when pressed, and it does it on a worker thread and writes the card so the next open is cheap again.
records.translation: Bannerinn **reads** er ákvarðanir; það talar ekki einn., sem er of lágt fyrir hvert heimsókn á skjánum. Svo :func:`spacr.seg_qc.read_digest` skiptir CSVs maska keyra þegar skrifað, dagsetur hver gegn maska stack hans, og rafa kortar eldri en maskar sínar sem út af daginu í stað þess að nota það. aðeins *Score maskar nú* butt scores eitthvað, aðeins þegar pressur, og það gerir það á bakgrunnsreiðslu einingu og skrifa kortina svo að næsta opnun er ódýr aftur.

records.context: Every call increments ``_refresh_gen``, including a call that finds the microscope field of view empty. That is what makes a read cancellable without being interruptible: nothing can stop the worker mid-``stat``, but its answer is checked against the question before it is painted and dropped when the source has moved on. Without it, clearing src hid the banner and the read still in flight put the old laboratory microplate's verdict straight back on application view under no name at all.
records.label: spacr.qt.prerun.SegQCBanner.refresh#4
records.source: Every call increments ``_refresh_gen``, including a call that finds the field empty. That is what makes a read cancellable without being interruptible: nothing can stop the worker mid-``stat``, but its answer is checked against the question before it is painted and dropped when the source has moved on. Without it, clearing src hid the banner and the read still in flight put the old plate's verdict straight back on screen under no name at all.
records.translation: Hver hringur er ``_refresh_gen``, þar á meðal hring sem finna mikroskópinn vöru. Það er það sem gerir lesing annullerandi án þess að vera hættir: ekkert getur stoppað vinnsluferli á miðjum ``stat``, en svarið er athugað gegn spurningu áður en það er mált og niður þegar kjarnan hefur farið áfram. Án þess, hreining src fela bannerið og lesun enn í flugi leggur gamall mikróplata dóm strax aftur á viðkomandi sýn undir neitt nafn alls.

records.context: A module that has been FOLDED into a host reaches the same machinery from the other end. Its own application view is not built any more, so ``install`` -- which answers for the application view's own key -- can never attach its panel; :func:`attach_folded` lets the host ask for it by name and keeps it hidden behind whatever the host uses to reveal the rest of that module. Mask Generation's tracking switch is the case it was written for.
records.translation: Múddur sem hefur verið FOLDED í hýsli fær sama vél frá öðrum endum. Sjálfur app sýning er ekki byggð neitt lengur, þannig að ``install`` - sem svarar fyrir app sýningu eigin lykill - getur aldrei tengjast panelinn; :func:`attach_folded` leyfir hýsil að spyrja það með nafni og haldið það gömlu fyrir hvað hýsil notar til að uppgötva aðrar múdd. records.context: ``clear CPU`` Releases parked background execution units that have since exited (:func:`spacr.qt.bridge.prune_parked_threads`), lets Qt's global pool retire its idle independent execution paths, and lowers spaCR's own library worker-count limits (torch, OpenCV) to a floor. It retires *idle* capacity only: work that is queued or executing is left exactly where it is.
records.label: spacr.qt.resource_cleanup#11
records.source: ``clear CPU`` Releases parked worker threads that have since exited (:func:`spacr.qt.bridge.prune_parked_threads`), lets Qt's global pool retire its idle threads, and lowers spaCR's own library thread counts (torch, OpenCV) to a floor. It retires *idle* capacity only: work that is queued or running is left exactly where it is.
records.translation: ``clear CPU`` útgáfa parkað bakgrunnsreiðslu einingar sem hafa síðan út (:func:`spacr.qt.bridge.prune_parked_threads`), leyfa Qt alþjóðlegur pool að hætta illt sjálfstætt reiðslu leiðir sínar, og draga spaCR eigin skrifstofu vinnsluferli-reiðanum (torch, OpenCV) til lofts. Það hættir *idle* tæki aðeins: vinnu sem er reiðan eða reiði er eftir nákvæmlega þar sem það er.

records.context: **A processing session in flight is never disturbed.** No queued job is dropped, no worker is cancelled, no worker pool is emptied of work that has not started yet. :func:`spacr.qt.bridge.registry` is *read* here and never cancelled.
records.label: spacr.qt.resource_cleanup#7
records.source: **A run in flight is never disturbed.** No queued job is dropped, no worker is cancelled, no thread pool is emptied of work that has not started yet. :func:`spacr.qt.bridge.registry` is *read* here and never cancelled.
records.translation: **A meðferð á fluginu er aldrei störst.** Engin vinnu er hættað, engin vinnsluferli eru hætti, enginn vinnsluferli er hætti úr vinnu sem hefur ekki byrjað enn. :func:`spacr.qt.bridge.registry` er *read* hér og aldrei hætti.

records.context: Run this on a worker. ``os.stat`` and ``shutil.disk_usage`` are the calls that wake a sleeping automount, and no cache can answer them without inventing the numbers, so the Qt caller hands this whole function to a :class:`~spacr.qt.job_runner.JobRunner` (:func:`spacr.qt.preferences._start_disk_report`). There the wait is unbounded on purpose: a worker is allowed to wait for a mount to wake up, and the drive table is complete.
records.label: spacr.qt.resource_cleanup.disk_report#2
records.source: RUN THIS ON A WORKER. ``os.stat`` and ``shutil.disk_usage`` are the calls that wake a sleeping automount, and no cache can answer them without inventing the numbers, so the Qt caller hands this whole function to a :class:`~spacr.qt.job_runner.JobRunner` (:func:`spacr.qt.preferences._start_disk_report`). There the wait is unbounded on purpose: a worker is allowed to wait for a mount to wake up, and the drive table is complete.
records.translation: Gerðu þetta á vinnsluferli. ``os.stat`` og ``shutil.disk_usage`` eru hringja sem vakna sveifandi bíll, og enginn cache getur svarað þeim án þess að uppgötva tölurnar, svo Qt hringjandi höndur þetta heila virkefni til :class:`~spacr.qt.job_runner.JobRunner` (:func:`spacr.qt.preferences._start_disk_report`). Þar er bíða óhætt á tilgangi: vinnsluferli er leyft að bíða fyrir fjallinn til að vakna, og bíðaþátturinn er fullkominn.

A click or ``Y`` confirms it (it becomes an ordinary label and wears a green tick); a right-click or ``N`` rejects it (it goes back to unanswered and wears a red cross); ``U`` undoes either. The bar above the structured-data name legend says so, and counts what the page and the column hold. Each judgement is written to the ``<column>_verdict`` column as ``+c`` or ``-c``, so it survives a restart, and the next Suggest round is handed the rejections to train on. See :meth:`AnnotateScreen._judge` and :func:`spacr.suggest.verdict_column`.
records.label: spacr.qt.screens.annotate#10
records.source: A suggestion is judged, not relabelled. A crop Suggest proposed a class for wears an amber ``?`` badge beside its dashed ring. The bar above the key legend says so, and counts what the page and the column hold. Each judgement is written to the ``<column>_verdict`` column as ``+c`` or ``-c``, so it survives a restart, and the next Suggest round is handed the rejections to train on. A klikk eða ``Y`` staðfestir það (þar verður venjulegt merki og bori græna tykki); hægri klukkuna eða ``N`` neita það (það fer aftur til ekki svarað og bori rödd kross); ``U`` er líka óþægilegt. Bærinn yfir byggð-data nafn leyndardómur segir svo, og talar það sem síðu og kolumnið hefur. Hver ákvarðan er skrifað í ``<column>_verdict`` stefnu sem ``+c`` eða ``-c``, þannig að það lifir endurstart, og næsta runda er sendur afslag til að þjálfa áfram. records.context: Lists and tuples are not a corner case. Containers are walked.

An earlier version of this method tested ``isinstance(value, str)`` and skipped everything else, which skipped exactly the two modules whose loaders never write a local path as a fallback -- so for those the publisher's path was the panel's only source of truth. Containers are walked.
records.translation: Listi og tuples eru ekki hjónaband. ``src`` klassify er list-valid og regressions ``count_data``, ``score_data`` og ``paired_data`` eru líka, og ``utils.load_settings`` breytir einhver CSV fruma sem byrjar með ``[``,``(`` eða ``{`` í alvöru Python efni. Fyrri útgáfa þessa aðferð prófaði ``isinstance(value, str)`` og skipt allt annað, sem skipti nákvæmlega tvö móddur sem ladders hafa aldrei skrifað staðbundna leið sem fallback - svo fyrir þá útgáfurins leið var bara orðin.

records.source: Converting renames files, for example ND2 files to ``plate1_A01_T0001F001L01A01Z01C01.tif``, and the new names no longer show which source file they came from, so a wrong well assignment can go unnoticed. records.source: **Off the GUI thread.** Scanning a plate's worth of ND2 headers takes seconds; converting takes minutes. records.context: **Background execution.** Each chunk, count, and export runs outside the GUI thread through :func:`spacr.qt.bridge.make_thread`, also used by workflow screens. records.source: **Off the GUI thread.** Every chunk, count and export goes through :func:`spacr.qt.bridge.make_thread`, the same helper the pipeline screens use, and each worker opens (and closes) its **own** sqlite connection — ``sqlite3`` objects are not shareable across threads. Jobs queue and run **one at a time**; see :meth:`DbBrowserScreen._run_job` for why two ``PipelineWorker``\ s must not overlap.

Hver vinnsluferli opnar og loka **a skilgreiða** sqlite tengsl; ``sqlite3`` hlutum er ekki hægt að deila milli útgáfu hliðar. Jobs rennir **sequentially**. :meth:`DbBrowserScreen._run_job` útskýrir hvers vegna tvö ``PipelineWorker``\ s getur ekki haldið yfir.

records.context: **Refusals and one-sided bounds are rows, not silence.** A laboratory microplate where three compounds fit and the fourth is cytotoxic at the top dose has four rows. The cytotoxic one says ``refused`` and carries the engine's message; a compound whose midpoint sits past the highest dose says ``unbounded`` and carries ``EC50 > 30 µM``, with an empty EC50 cell. Neither is dropped from the table, so a refused or unbounded fit is not shown as missing data.
records.label: spacr.qt.screens.dose_response#3
records.source: **Refusals and one-sided bounds are rows, not silence.** A plate where three compounds fit and the fourth is cytotoxic at the top dose has four rows. The cytotoxic one says ``refused`` and carries the engine's message; a compound whose midpoint sits past the highest dose says ``unbounded`` and carries ``EC50 > 30 µM``, with an empty EC50 cell. Neither is dropped from the table, so a refused or unbounded fit is not shown as missing data.
records.translation: **Refusals og einhversta hliðar eru ránir, ekki þögn.** Mikróplata í plötu þar sem þrír samsetningar passa og fjórða er cytotoxic á toppdósi hefur fjórar ránar. Cytotoxic einn segir ``refused`` og bori skilaboð motorins; samsetur sem miðpunkti sem situr yfir hærsta dosi segir ``unbounded`` og bori ``EC50 > 30 µM``, með leitt EC50 frumu. Ekki er neitt út úr borðinu, þannig að neitt neitt eða óhneigð er ekki sýnt sem saknað gögnum.

records.context: Embeddings — a label-free vector for every object, beside the measured panel.

records.translation: Inbeddings - merkjalaus vektor fyrir hvert objekt, við hliðarpanna.

records.context: **The encoder is identified with the checksum of its weights.** The processing session summary carries the model-zoo entry from :func:`spacr.embeddings.encoder_entry` -- backbone, policy and the digest of the weights on this machine -- because two processing sessions' dimension 17 are the same number and not the same thing unless all three match.
records.label: spacr.qt.screens.embeddings#10
records.source: **The encoder is identified with the checksum of its weights.** The run summary carries the model-zoo entry from :func:`spacr.embeddings.encoder_entry` -- backbone, policy and the digest of the weights on this machine -- because two runs' dimension 17 are the same number and not the same thing unless all three match.
records.translation: **Kóderinn er þekkt með athygli vægi síns.** Áhuggjörð uppsetningu bjarga mönnun-zoo inntali frá :func:`spacr.embeddings.encoder_entry` - bakgrunni, lögum og svæði af þygi á þessari vél - vegna þess að tvö meðferð uppsetningar 17 eru sömu fjölda og ekki sama hluti nema allar þremur tengjast.

records.context: **What it is for.** Giving every object a vector that no label went into. The measured panel says how big a cell is and how bright each stain was; an embedding describes what the cell looks like, in a few hundred numbers a pretrained backbone produces without being told what to look for. It complements the panel rather than replacing it: a phenotype that no measured column captures can still be represented in the vector.
records.label: spacr.qt.screens.embeddings#3
records.source: **What it is for.** Giving every object a vector that no label went into. The measured panel says how big a cell is and how bright each stain was; an embedding describes what the cell looks like, in a few hundred numbers a pretrained backbone produces without being told what to look for. It complements the panel rather than replacing it: a phenotype that no measured column captures can still be represented in the vector.
records.translation: **Hvað er það fyrir.** Gefur hvert hlut vektor sem engin tákn kom inn. Miðanlegur panel segir hversu mikla fruma er og hversu ljósi hver stain var; innbyggingu lýsir hvernig fruma líður út, í nokkrum hundruðum tölum framkvæma fyrirþróun hægur án þess að segja hvað að leita að.

records.context: **The channel policy is the first control on the screen.** How channels are combined must not be decided implicitly by whatever the backbone expects. Per-channel encoding keeps the channel in every column name and costs N forward passes; projection mixes the channels into three and costs one. Those produce columns of identical width and dtype that mean entirely different things, so the screen makes the choice explicit and says what each one costs.
records.label: spacr.qt.screens.embeddings#8
records.source: **The channel policy is the first control on the screen.** How channels are combined must not be decided implicitly by whatever the backbone expects. Per-channel encoding keeps the channel in every column name and costs N forward passes; projection mixes the channels into three and costs one. Those produce columns of identical width and dtype that mean entirely different things, so the screen makes the choice explicit and says what each one costs.
records.translation: **Rásamyndin er fyrsti stjórnun á skjánum.** Hvernig rásir eru sameiginlegir ætti ekki að ákveða í óþekktum af því hvað bakgrunni vantar. Per-rásakódingu halda rásina í hverjum kolumna nafn og kostnaður N framur; sýning blanda rásina í þrjá og kostar einn. Þeir framleiða kolumnar á sama breidd og dtype sem þýðir alveg mismunandi hluti, þannig að skjár gerir valinn útskýrt og segir hvað hver kostar.

records.context: Pick an extracted image region source and a channel policy, and embed every object.

records.context: The laboratory microplate drawing is shared where it can be. The square, the constant it is pitched at and the row/column headers come from :mod:`spacr.qt.widgets.plate_map_picker` rather than being declared a second time here; the two laboratory microplates had already drifted apart once. What cannot be shared is the well itself, and the difference is functional: the picker's well is a checkable ``QPushButton`` whose checked state IS the selection and which paints itself from a fixed pair of colours, while this one is a ``QLabel`` carrying a role, an edge mark, a name and a condition, painted by the theme through the properties below -- a laboratory microplate map that says what each well holds rather than only whether it is chosen.
records.label: spacr.qt.screens.experiment_design#7
records.source: The plate drawing is shared where it can be. The square, the constant it is pitched at and the row/column headers come from :mod:`spacr.qt.widgets.plate_map_picker` rather than being declared a second time here; the two plates had already drifted apart once. What cannot be shared is the well itself, and the difference is functional: the picker's well is a checkable ``QPushButton`` whose checked state IS the selection and which paints itself from a fixed pair of colours, while this one is a ``QLabel`` carrying a role, an edge mark, a name and a condition, painted by the theme through the properties below -- a plate map that says what each well holds rather than only whether it is chosen.
records.translation: Mikróplata málið er að deila þar sem það getur verið. Kjarta, stöðuna sem það er ritað á og höfuð / kolumna kemur frá :mod:`spacr.qt.widgets.plate_map_picker` í stað þess að vera sagt annað sinn hér; tveir mikrókra málið hefur þegar dreifið saman einu sinni. Það sem ekki er hægt að deilla er jólin sjálfur, og munurinn er virkilega: Pickers brunnur er athyglislegt ``QPushButton`` sem athygli staður er úrval og sem illt sjálfan sig frá fasteignum parum litum, en þetta er ``QLabel`` með hlutverk, eyðimörkin, nafn og tilstand, málin í gegnum eiginleika hér að neðan - mikróslata mála sem segir hvað hver góður heldur heldur en hvort það er valið.

records.context: :mod:`spacr.foreign` does the work; this screen is for the step that needs review. A foreign ``Area`` can be in µm² where spaCR's ``cell_area`` is in px², so an unreviewed mapping can give values that look plausible and are wrong by a factor of several hundred. So the mapping table is the middle of the screen, it is **editable**, and every edit re-runs the conflict and unit checks in place.
records.label: spacr.qt.screens.foreign#1
records.source: :mod:`spacr.foreign` does the work; this screen is for the step that needs review. A foreign ``Area`` can be in µm² where spaCR's ``cell_area`` is in px², so an unreviewed mapping can give values that look plausible and are wrong by a factor of several hundred. So the mapping table is the middle of the screen, it is **editable**, and every edit re-runs the conflict and unit checks in place.
records.translation: :mod:`spacr.foreign` gerir vinnu; þetta skjár er fyrir skref sem þarf að skoða. Frjáls ``Area`` getur verið í µm² þar sem spaCR ``cell_area`` er í px², þannig að unreviewed mapping getur gefið verð sem líta vel og eru rangt af tegundum af nokkrum hundruðum. Þannig er mappingu tólin miðjan skjár, það er **reitable**, og hvert útgáfur endurskoða stríðið og einkefni athuga á staðnum.

records.context: Structurally this is the sibling of :mod:`spacr.qt.widgets.live_preview`: a self-contained :class:`QWidget` that owns its own controls, runs the expensive work on a :class:`QThread`, streams results back over signals, reports every failure inline (never in a modal — a QMessageBox hangs a headless run), and pushes a chosen configuration back into the host application view's settings panel through a callback the host registers. Host application views embed it with :func:`build_hyperparam_card`, exactly the way the Mask application view embeds the live preview, and toggle it with a label reading "Hyperparameter search" where the Mask application view's says "Live".
records.label: spacr.qt.screens.hyperparam#1
records.source: Structurally this is the sibling of :mod:`spacr.qt.widgets.live_preview`: a self-contained :class:`QWidget` that owns its own controls, runs the expensive work on a :class:`QThread`, streams results back over signals, reports every failure inline (never in a modal — a QMessageBox hangs a headless run), and pushes a chosen configuration back into the host screen's settings panel through a callback the host registers. Host screens embed it with :func:`build_hyperparam_card`, exactly the way the Mask screen embeds the live preview, and toggle it with a label reading "Hyperparameter search" where the Mask screen's says "Live".
records.translation: Struktúrlega þetta er bróðirinn af :mod:`spacr.qt.widgets.live_preview`: sjálfstætt :class:`QWidget` sem eigir eigin stjórn, Það er kostarlegt að vinna á :class:`QThread`. fljótur koma aftur yfir signa, búnir um hverja mistök í tengslum (einhver í modal - QMessageBox hangar keyrslulaus renn), og snúir valið uppsetningu aftur inn í setningarpanna veitingahúsins í gegnum callback hýsilskrár. Hosta notkun sýningar tengist það með :func:`build_hyperparam_card`, nákvæmlega þannig að sýning notkun Mask tengist live sýning, og taka það með tákn lesa "Hyperparameter search" þar sem sýning Notkun Mask segir "Live".

records.source: A measurement scatter holds thousands of points. A point's coordinates show that an object is unusual, for example at (0.9, 12.4), but not whether it is a real phenotype, a debris fragment or two cells segmented as one; telling these apart needs the crop.

records.context: So: **hover shows the crop, click opens it.** The click goes through :func:`spacr.qt.linked_selection.open_objects`, so this application view does not import the annotation grid and the grid grows no method for it.

records.translation: Þannig: **hover sýnir myndskurði, smellur opnar það.** Klíkurinn fer í gegnum :func:`spacr.qt.linked_selection.open_objects`, þannig að þessi sýning á notkunin myndi ekki inn notandi net og neturinn mun ekki veita til þess.

records.context: A hover handler runs sixty-plus times a second and a PNG decode costs milliseconds, so the obvious implementation — decode the extracted image region under the cursor in ``mouseMoveEvent`` — produces a plot that lags behind the mouse. Three measures keep hover responsive:
records.label: spacr.qt.screens.image_scatter#4
records.source: A hover handler runs sixty-plus times a second and a PNG decode costs milliseconds, so the obvious implementation — decode the crop under the cursor in ``mouseMoveEvent`` — produces a plot that lags behind the mouse. Three measures keep hover responsive:
records.translation: A hover handlegur fer sjöunda-plus sinnum á sekúnd og PNG dekóða kostar millisekundum, þannig að augljóslega framkvæmd — dekóður af myndskurðum myndum svæðum undir cursor í ``mouseMoveEvent`` — framleiðir mál sem liggur bak mus.

records.context: Decoding is behind a short debounce and an LRU (:class:`spacr.qt.crop_thumbs.CropThumbnails`). Sweeping the cursor across a cluster decodes what the cursor *stopped* on, not everything it crossed; an extracted image region already in the cache appears with no delay at all.
records.label: spacr.qt.screens.image_scatter#7
records.source: Decoding is behind a short debounce and an LRU (:class:`spacr.qt.crop_thumbs.CropThumbnails`). Sweeping the cursor across a cluster decodes what the cursor *stopped* on, not everything it crossed; a crop already in the cache appears with no delay at all.
records.translation: Þekkingu er fyrir stuttum niðurstaðanum og LRU (:class:`spacr.qt.crop_thumbs.CropThumbnails`). Svíking ákur yfir klúster dekodir það sem cursor *stopped* á, ekki allt sem það krossist; myndskurður mynd svæðis þegar í skjölinu birtist með engin hættu alls.

records.context: Image UMAP, Image Scatter and PCA provide complementary projections of the same objects. Image Scatter plots two measured variables with extracted image region previews and linked selection. PCA provides feature selection, a scree plot, a loadings biplot, local filtering and CSV export.

records.source: Image UMAP, Image Scatter and PCA provide complementary projections of the same objects. Image Scatter plots two measured variables with crop previews and linked selection. PCA provides feature selection, a scree plot, a loadings biplot, local filtering and CSV export.
records.translation: Image UMAP, Image Scatter og PCA bjóða upp á viðbótar sýningar af sömu hlutum. Image Skatter safnar tveimur mættum breytingum með myndskurði myndarregion forritum og tengd val. PCA bjóður upp á eiginleika, skreyting plöt, laddings biplot, staðbundna flutning og CSV útvinning.

records.context: Lineage screen: the containment tree of cells, nuclei and pathogens.
records.label: spacr.qt.screens.lineage#0
records.source: Lineage screen: the containment tree of cells, nuclei and pathogens.
records.translation: Linear skref: þremur af frumunum, kjarna og sýklum.

records.context: In ``measurements.db``, ``nucleus`` and ``pathogen`` rows carry a ``cell_id`` naming the cell they sit inside (:data:`spacr.schema.CHILD_OBJECT_TABLES`). This application view shows those links as a tree, so questions such as which cells are uninfected, which pathogen is implausibly large for the cell around it, and which nucleus belongs to no cell at all can be answered by inspection.
records.label: spacr.qt.screens.lineage#1
records.source: In ``measurements.db``, ``nucleus`` and ``pathogen`` rows carry a ``cell_id`` naming the cell they sit inside (:data:`spacr.schema.CHILD_OBJECT_TABLES`). This screen shows those links as a tree, so questions such as which cells are uninfected, which pathogen is implausibly large for the cell around it, and which nucleus belongs to no cell at all can be answered by inspection.
records.translation: Í ``measurements.db``, ``nucleus`` og ``pathogen`` ránir eiga ``cell_id`` að nafnið á frumunni sem þeir sitja inni (:data:`spacr.schema.CHILD_OBJECT_TABLES`). Þessi sýning á notkun sýnir þessar tengsl eins og tré, svo spurningar eins og hvaða frumur eru ekki smittir, hvaða sýkill er óþægilegt stór fyrir frumu í kringum það, og hvaðan kjarn tilheyrir engin frumur alls getur verið svarað með athygli.

records.context: A child whose ``cell_id`` names no cell is dropped by every join in the codebase. It is not noise: it means the nucleus mask found an object the cell mask did not, which is a segmentation disagreement worth looking at. It gets its own list here, with the same double-click-to-open, so these objects can be reviewed without writing SQL.
records.label: spacr.qt.screens.lineage#4
records.source: A child whose ``cell_id`` names no cell is dropped by every join in the codebase. It is not noise: it means the nucleus mask found an object the cell mask did not, which is a segmentation disagreement worth looking at. It gets its own list here, with the same double-click-to-open, so these objects can be reviewed without writing SQL.
records.translation: Barnið sem ``cell_id`` heitir engin cella er kastað af hverjum tengingu í kóddabáði. Það er ekki rök: það þýðir að kjarnagrímu fann hlut sem cella maska ekki, sem er skilgreiningu mismunandi sem vantar að horfa á. Það fær eigin lista hér, með sama tvöklika-til-auka, þannig að þessar hlutur geta verið skoðað án þess að skrifa SQL.

records.context: ``False`` reads inline, so a test drives the screen without a background execution unit and gets the same calls in the same order.
records.label: spacr.qt.screens.lineage.LineageScreen#1
records.source: ``False`` reads inline, so a test drives the screen without a worker thread and gets the same calls in the same order.
records.translation: ``False`` lætur í línu, þannig að próf dreifir skjár án bakgrunnsreiðslu einkefni og fær sömu hringjum í sama orði.

records.context: **Normally empty.** The object key carries the object type, so a cell's nucleus 1 and its pathogen 1 are two keys. The check is kept to report a regression in which keys collide again; without it, "opening four objects showed three extracted image regions" would have no explanation on screen.
records.label: spacr.qt.screens.lineage.LineageScreen.collision_note#1
records.source: **Normally empty.** The object key carries the object type, so a cell's nucleus 1 and its pathogen 1 are two keys. The check is kept to report a regression in which keys collide again; without it, "opening four objects showed three crops" would have no explanation on screen.
records.translation: **Normally empty.** Object key bori objekt type, þannig að kjarnann 1 og sýkill 1 er tvö key. Verið er haldið til að rafa um regressíu þar sem lykillir stökkva aftur; án þess, "öppni fjórar hlutum sýndi þrjú myndskurðir myndar svæðum" myndi ekki hafa útskýringu á skjánum.

records.context: De-duplicated while keeping order: selecting a cell and one of its pathogens must not open that pathogen twice.
records.label: spacr.qt.screens.lineage.LineageScreen.family_keys#1
records.source: De-duplicated while keeping order: selecting a cell and one of its pathogens must not open that pathogen twice.
records.translation: De-duplicated meðan að halda orði: valinn af frumu og einn af sýkli hans ætti ekki að opna þessi sýkill tvö sinnum.

records.context: The de-duplication is on the shared key, which is what the routing contract takes. That key carries the object type, so a cell's nucleus 1 and pathogen 1 stay two keys; if keys ever collide, fewer keys than objects are returned and :meth:`collision_note` reports it on application view.
records.label: spacr.qt.screens.lineage.LineageScreen.family_keys#2
records.source: The de-duplication is on the shared key, which is what the routing contract takes. That key carries the object type, so a cell's nucleus 1 and pathogen 1 stay two keys; if keys ever collide, fewer keys than objects are returned and :meth:`collision_note` reports it on screen.
records.translation: Að de-duplication er á sameiginlegri key, sem er það sem leiðandi samning tekur.Þetta key bjarga efni tegund, þannig að kjarna 1 og sýkill 1 í frumu verður tvö key; ef keyir stökk, færri keyir en objekt eru aftur og :meth:`collision_note` rafa það á umsókn sýn.

records.translation: Einn folded móddur, eins og allan skrin það var, plus það sem hýsilinn bætir.

records.context: A fold that reimplemented the module it replaced would keep whatever the person doing the folding happened to think of and quietly drop the rest. So the button opens the module's OWN widget: every control, every worker, every drop target it had as a tile is what arrives, and the only thing that changed is where it is opened from.
records.label: spacr.qt.screens.make_masks.FoldedModulePanel#1
records.source: A fold that reimplemented the module it replaced would keep whatever the person doing the folding happened to think of and quietly drop the rest. So the button opens the module's OWN widget: every control, every worker, every drop target it had as a tile is what arrives, and the only thing that changed is where it is opened from.
records.translation: A fold sem endurtekinir mól sem hann skiptir myndi halda hvað sem maður sem gerir folding gerðist til að hugsa um og hljóðlega drop restinn. records.context: Closing the panel is not enough. A module polls the machine's RAM and GPU on a background execution unit, and Qt answers an executing QThread being destroyed by aborting the process — so the module's own close handler, which drains that worker, has to execute. records.source: Closing the panel is not enough. A module polls the machine's RAM and GPU on a worker thread, and Qt answers a running QThread being destroyed by aborting the process — so the module's own close handler, which drains that worker, has to run. A page nested inside another module's tabs never gets one from Qt, which is why they are closed by hand here.
records.translation: Að loka panelinn er ekki nóg. Síðasta síðu inn í tabum annarra múdulinn fær aldrei einn frá Qt, sem er ástæðan fyrir því að þeir eru lokað með hönd hér.

records.context: Two kinds of fold are used here, and they change this screen differently. See :data:`CATEGORY_FOLDS`, :data:`PAGE_FOLDS` and :func:`install_ops_switch`.

records.context: **Nothing here writes.** No repeat-execution button, no "mark as fresh", no delete. The screen answers a question; acting on the answer is the module's job, and a one-click execute again wired to a graph is how somebody overwrites the artifact they were trying to check.

records.source: **Nothing here writes.** No re-run button, no "mark as fresh", no delete. The screen answers a question; acting on the answer is the module's job, and a one-click re-run wired to a graph is how somebody overwrites the artifact they were trying to check.

records.context: **And neither does opening the application view, nor opening its folder chooser.** Two things here take a path the user typed on some *other* application view: the search folders :func:`make_project_browser_screen` seeds from the recent-source list, and the folder the "Add folder…" dialog starts in. Neither is checked with ``os.path.isdir`` on the main GUI execution path: measured on one workstation, one such folder was under an ``autofs`` mount whose share was asleep, and a single ``isdir`` on it had not returned after twenty seconds, freezing the whole application with no traceback. Both ask :mod:`spacr.qt.path_probe`, which answers from a cache and stats in the background. Those two are the whole inventory: the walk executes on a worker, and every column, note and detail line the application view draws is rendered from the frozen :class:`spacr.projects.ProjectSummary` that walk already returned, so filling the table and the detail pane reads nothing.
records.label: spacr.qt.screens.project_browser#6
records.source: **And neither does opening the screen, nor opening its folder chooser.** Two things here take a path the user typed on some *other* screen: the search folders :func:`make_project_browser_screen` seeds from the recent-source list, and the folder the "Add folder…" dialog starts in. Neither is checked with ``os.path.isdir`` on the GUI thread: measured on one workstation, one such folder was under an ``autofs`` mount whose share was asleep, and a single ``isdir`` on it had not returned after twenty seconds, freezing the whole application with no traceback. Both ask :mod:`spacr.qt.path_probe`, which answers from a cache and stats in the background. Those two are the whole inventory: the walk runs on a worker, and every column, note and detail line the screen draws is rendered from the frozen :class:`spacr.projects.ProjectSummary` that walk already returned, so filling the table and the detail pane reads nothing.
records.translation: **Og ekki opna notkun, né opna mappinn valandi.** Tveir hlutir hér taka leið notandinn skrifað á nokkrum *other* notkun: leitað mappingar :func:`make_project_browser_screen` semir frá nýjustu kjarna listanum, og mappurinn "Add folder…" samskipti byrjar í. Ekki er neitt athugað með ``os.path.isdir`` á helstu GUI framkvæmdspjall: mættur á einn vinnustaður, einn af slíkum skálum var undir ``autofs`` fjall sem hlutverki þeirra var svefnun, og einn ``isdir`` á það hafði ekki komist eftir tíu sekúndur, fræsað allan notkun með engum traceback. Bæði spyrja :mod:`spacr.qt.path_probe`, sem svara frá skjöl og tölur í bakgrunni. Þessir tveir eru allan uppsetningu: gangurinn fer á vinnsluferli, og hver kolumn, notan og upplýsingar stefnu útgáfu notan er gefið frá frystu :class:`spacr.projects.ProjectSummary` sem gangurinn hefur þegar komist aftur, þannig að fylgjandi borðinn og upplýsingarnar leitar ekkert.

records.context: It **reads**; it does not score. The rule is :mod:`spacr.qt.prerun`'s, and that module says why: opening a plate's masks costs seconds to minutes, which is too slow to repeat on every visit. So the reads go through a fingerprint cache -- one listdir and one stat per artifact -- and the parse only happens when something on disk has actually changed.

records.source: It **reads**; it does not score. So the reads go through a fingerprint cache -- one listdir and one stat per artifact -- and the parse only happens when something on disk has actually changed.
records.translation: Það **reads**; það er ekki skólanir. regla er :mod:`spacr.qt.prerun` s, og þessi módul segir hvers vegna: opna maskar á plötu kostar sekúnd til mínútur, sem er of langan til að endurtekin á hverjum heimsókn.

records.context: `path_probe` is not used for the folder guard. records.source: `path_probe` is not used for the folder guard. records.translation: `path_probe` er ekki notuð fyrir mappinn. Það svör optimistically, þannig að það gæti aðeins alltaf sagt "go on and read", sem vinnsluferli þá athygli á alla hátt; annað gárd á heiminum GUI útferð myndi aðeins leyfa tveimur svörum að skilja.

records.context: **Methods & Results** builds the processing-session digest -- package versions, timings, seed and error policy, per-module parameters parsed out of the emitted macro, the segmentation verdict, artifact counts, held-out metrics -- drafts the two sections from it and then mechanically checks every number in the draft back against the digest. records.source: **Methods & Results** builds the run digest -- package versions, timings, seed and error policy, per-module parameters parsed out of the emitted macro, the segmentation verdict, artifact counts, held-out metrics -- drafts the two sections from it and then mechanically checks every number in the draft back against the digest. It opens seeded with the project the regression screen is already pointed at, so the path it otherwise asks the user to type is filled in.
records.translation: **Methods & Results** byggir meðferð-sessions digest - pakka útgáfur, tími, sæd og mistök stjórn, per-module parsed út af útgáfu macro, segmenda dóm, artifact tákn, hold-out metrics - útgáfa tveimur hluta frá því og þá meðileg athuga hvert tölur í uppgáfu aftur gegn digest. Það opnar sæd með verkefni regressions skjár er þegar sýnt á, þannig að leiðin sem annars biðja notandi til stafa er fyllt í.

records.context: A settings CSV, a restored session or a recipe belongs to one of the two modules, and applying it to both would write a training folder into the Apply tab's path field — the one thing the two-field split exists to prevent. The tab is chosen by which one owns more of the structured-data names that the OTHER one does not have, so ``n_epochs`` picks Train and ``flow_threshold`` picks Apply; a key-value mapping that distinguishes neither goes to the tab already on application view. The chosen tab is raised, so the settings are visible where they landed.

records.source: A settings CSV, a restored session or a recipe belongs to one of the two modules, and applying it to both would write a training folder into the Apply tab's path field — the one thing the two-field split exists to prevent. The tab is chosen by which one owns more of the keys the OTHER one does not have, so ``n_epochs`` picks Train and ``flow_threshold`` picks Apply; a dict that distinguishes neither goes to the tab already on screen. The chosen tab is raised, so the settings are visible where they landed.
records.translation: A setting CSV, endurnýjandi tímapunktur eða uppskrift er hluti af einn af tveimur mælikum, og að nota það á báðum myndi skrifa þjálfunarfólkið í leiðræðanum Apply tab - það eina sem tvö reiturinn er til að koma í veg fyrir. Tab er valið með því að einn eigandi meira af byggð gögnum nafnum sem annar hefur ekki, svo ``n_epochs`` picks Train og ``flow_threshold`` picks Apply; key-value mapping sem skilgreinir ekki einu sinni fara á skálinn þegar á app sýn.

records.context: **The diff is bucketed, never flat.** It renders :func:`spacr.train_compare.diff_settings`, which reuses the provenance bucketing from :mod:`spacr.run_journal`: environment drift (paths, hosts, worker counts) is shown in its own bucket instead of being counted as something the user changed, and schema drift is summarised. When two processing sessions match, the table says "no differences" in words rather than going blank.
records.label: spacr.qt.screens.train_compare#7
records.source: **The diff is bucketed, never flat.** It renders :func:`spacr.train_compare.diff_settings`, which reuses the provenance bucketing from :mod:`spacr.run_journal`: environment drift (paths, hosts, worker counts) is shown in its own bucket instead of being counted as something the user changed, and schema drift is summarised. When two runs match, the table says "no differences" in words rather than going blank.
records.translation: **Dif er bucketed, aldrei flatt.** Það gengur :func:`spacr.train_compare.diff_settings`, sem endurnýta afleiðing bucketing frá :mod:`spacr.run_journal`: umhverfis drif (þáttar, hermenn, vinnsluferli tölur) er sýnt í eigin bucket í stað þess að vera ritað sem eitthvað sem notandinn breytti, og skema drif er sumnað. Þegar tvö meðferð árás saman, tólin segir "no differences" í orðum en ekki fara blank.

records.context: A separate window, not the main one made full application view. Hiding spaCR's own widgets and restoring them afterwards means remembering what was visible, what had focus, which docks were open and what the splitters were set to -- and getting any of it wrong leaves the user's layout rearranged by something that was meant to be a screensaver. A window of its own has nothing to restore: it is closed and the application is exactly as it was.
records.label: spacr.qt.screensaver#1
records.source: A SEPARATE WINDOW, not the main one made full screen. Hiding spaCR's own widgets and restoring them afterwards means remembering what was visible, what had focus, which docks were open and what the splitters were set to -- and getting any of it wrong leaves the user's layout rearranged by something that was meant to be a screensaver. A window of its own has nothing to restore: it is closed and the application is exactly as it was.
records.translation: Að fela spaCR eigin widgets og endurheimta þá síðar þýðir að muna hvað var sýnilegt, hvað hafði áherslu, hvaða dúkkur voru opnar og hvaða skjás voru sett á - og að fá hvaða af þeim rangt leyfir notandi uppsetningu aftur með eitthvað sem var áætlað að vera skreynsla.

records.context: A spaCR execution has about two hundred setting names. An ungrouped comparison of two executions can mix one Cellpose setting with one laboratory plate-map column. Group the differences under the settings-panel headings so the user can see at once: *the change was in Cellpose*.

records.source: A spaCR run carries around two hundred keys, so an ungrouped diff of two runs that differ in one Cellpose knob and one plate-map column reads as an undifferentiated list. Grouping under the same headings the settings panel uses makes it answerable at a glance: *the change was in Cellpose*.
records.translation: A spaCR framkvæmd hefur um tvö hundruð setningar. A óþekkt samanburður af tveimur útkomum getur blandað einn Cellpose setting með einn platan plata-mapp kolumn. Sumir munur undir setningarpanel heitu svo notandi getur séð á einu sinni: *s breyting var í Cellpose*.

records.context: Owns no settings state of its own — it reads the screen's ``SettingsWidgets`` model and shows or hides rows that already exist. Hiding rather than rebuilding is what keeps a half-typed value alive across a filter change, which a rebuild would silently discard.

records.source: Owns no settings state of its own — it reads the screen's ``SettingsWidgets`` model and shows or hides rows that already exist. Hiding rather than rebuilding is what keeps a half-typed value alive across a filter change, which a rebuild would silently discard.
records.translation: Eigir engin staðsetningar eigin — það lesa ``SettingsWidgets`` myndavél á skjánum og sýnir eða fela ránir sem eru þegar til. Hiding í stað þess að endurbyggja er það sem hallar hálf-typed verð lifandi á gegnum fljótara breyting, sem endurbygging myndi hljóðlega fjarlægja.

records.context: Every generator is *reproducible*: identical inputs give byte-identical output on any machine, so two people comparing "the demo fails here" look at the same pixels. records.source: A screen root is a QSS scope: rules installed there reach that screen and its descendants, and applying them before the root is shown preserves the same first-paint contract without touching Home or any previously opened module.

records.context: The suffix contains every registered block absent from the application sheet, in registry order, rather than only ``names``.  This keeps blocks imported by a screen's dependencies together and means a later call can replace one complete suffix instead of stacking fragments with different preference values.  ``names`` remains the caller's documentation of the blocks it requires; omitting it is the MainWindow screen-host path.
